value.zh: 諸侯有不貢士謂之不率正，一不適謂之過，再不適謂之傲，三不適謂之誣。
value.en: Lords who sent no talent were 'not rectifying'; one miss was a fault, two arrogance, three deceit.
value.literal: Feudal lords who did not present scholars were called 'not leading correctly'; one failure was called 'fault,' a second 'arrogance,' a third 'deceit.'

value.zh: 誣者，天子絀之，一絀以爵，再絀以地，三絀而爵地畢」也。
value.en: After three failures the throne stripped rank, then land, then both.'
value.literal: The deceitful—the Son of Heaven degraded them: first degradation by rank, second by land, third and rank and land were exhausted."

value.zh: 五禮之別，二曰凶。
value.en: Among the five canonical rituals, the second category is mourning for the dead.
value.literal: Of the five kinds of ritual, the second is called 'inauspicious' (mourning).

value.zh: 自天子至於庶人，身體髮膚，受之父母，其理既均，其情亦等，生則養，死則哀，故曰三年之喪，天下之達禮者也。
value.en: From the sovereign to the humblest subject, flesh and hair come from one's parents; the duty is the same and the grief no different—while they live we sustain them, when they die we mourn them. Hence the canon calls three years' mourning the rite that runs through all the world.
value.literal: From the Son of Heaven down to the common people, body, skin, and hair are received from father and mother; the principle is uniform and the feeling equal—in life they nurture, in death they mourn; therefore it is said that three years' mourning is the penetrating rite of the realm.

value.zh: 漢禮，天子崩，自不豫至於登遐及葬，喪紀之制，與夫三代變易。
value.en: Han court precedent for an emperor's death—from the first illness through the lying-in-state to interment—shifted its mourning code across the Xia, Shang, and Zhou models.
value.literal: Under Han ritual, when the Son of Heaven collapsed, from the first illness through the final journey to burial, the mourning regulations changed with the Three Dynasties.

value.zh: 魏晉以來，大體同漢。
value.en: From the Wei through the Jin, the dynasty largely kept Han practice.
value.literal: From Wei and Jin onward, the broad pattern matched Han.

value.zh: 然自漢文革喪禮之制，後代遵之，無復三年之禮。
value.en: Yet once Emperor Wen of Han pared the mourning statutes, every succeeding age copied his shortcut, and the full three-year observance disappeared.
value.literal: Yet from Emperor Wen of Han's reform of mourning regulations, later ages followed it and no longer practiced three years' mourning.

value.zh: 及魏武臨終，遺令「天下尚未安定，未得遵古。
value.en: When Wei Wu was near death, he left a command: 'All under Heaven is not yet settled; I cannot follow antiquity.
value.literal: When Wei Wu was near death, he left a command: 'All under Heaven is not yet settled; I cannot follow antiquity.

value.zh: 百官當臨中者，十五舉音，葬畢便除。
value.en: For the hundred officials who should attend at the central halt, raise the dirge fifteen times; when burial is finished, remove mourning at once.
value.literal: For the hundred officials who should attend at the central halt, raise the dirge fifteen times; when burial is finished, remove mourning at once.

value.zh: 其將兵屯戍者，不得離部。」
value.en: Those who command troops on garrison may not leave their commands.'
value.literal: Those who command troops on garrison may not leave their commands.'

value.zh: 魏武以正月庚子崩，辛丑即殯，是月丁卯葬，是為不逾月也。
value.en: Cao Cao died on the gengzi day of the first month; by xinchou the bier stood ready; dingmao that same month saw the interment—mourning lifted inside a single month.
value.literal: Wei Wu died on gengzi in the first month; on xinchou he was encoffined; on dingmao that same month he was buried—this is what is meant by 'not exceeding one month.'

value.zh: 漢魏故事，大喪及大臣之喪，執紼者輓歌。
value.en: Han and Wei custom had catafalque bearers chant pulling-dirges at imperial funerals and at those of great ministers.
value.literal: Han-Wei precedent: great mourning and great ministers' mourning—those holding tow-ropes sang dirges.

value.zh: 新禮以為輓歌出於漢武帝役人之勞歌，聲哀切，遂以為送終之禮。
value.en: The New Rites traced those laments to corvée labor songs under Emperor Wu—voices sharp with grief—and showed how they had hardened into funeral practice.
value.literal: The New Rites held dirges arose from Han Emperor Wu's corvée people's labor songs—sound mournful and piercing—thereupon taken as seeing-off-the-end rite.

value.zh: 雖音曲摧愴，非經典所制，違禮設銜枚之義。
value.en: However wrenching the tunes, they are nowhere mandated in the classics and violate the spirit of biting wooden gag-bits to keep silence.
value.literal: Though melody is crushing-grief—not fashioned by classics—contravenes the rites' meaning of mouth-plugs.

value.zh: 方在號慕，不宜以歌為名。
value.en: Mid-wail for the dead, nothing should parade under the label of "song."
value.literal: Just now in wailing longing—not fitting to take 'song' as name.

value.zh: 除，不輓歌。
value.en: The reform abolished pulling-dirges altogether.
value.literal: Removed—no dirges.

value.zh: 摯虞以為：「輓歌因倡和而為摧愴之聲，銜枚所以全哀，此亦以感眾。
value.en: Zhi Yu held: "Dirges through lead-and-chorus become crushing sounds—mouth-plugs thereby preserve mourning—this too thereby moves the crowd.
value.literal: Zhi Yu held: "Dirges through lead-and-chorus become crushing sounds—mouth-plugs thereby preserve mourning—this too thereby moves the crowd.

value.zh: 雖非經典所載，是歷代故事。
value.en: Though not carried in classics—it is successive dynasties' precedent.
value.literal: Though not carried in classics—it is successive dynasties' precedent.

value.zh: 《詩》稱『君子作歌，惟以告哀』，以歌為名，亦無所嫌。
value.en: The Odes state 'the gentleman makes song—only to declare grief'—to take song as name—also nothing blameworthy.
value.literal: The Odes state 'the gentleman makes song—only to declare grief'—to take song as name—also nothing blameworthy.

value.zh: 宜定新禮如舊。」
value.en: It is fitting to fix the New Rites as of old."
value.literal: It is fitting to fix the New Rites as of old."

value.zh: 詔從之，
value.en: The court accepted his opinion.
value.literal: An edict followed this.

value.zh: 愍懷太子
value.en: Crown Prince Minhuai
value.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai

value.zh: 湣懷太子遹，字熙祖，惠帝長子，母曰謝才人。
value.en: Sima Yu, styled Xizu, was Emperor Hui's firstborn—his mother was Lady Xie of Talented rank.
value.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.

value.zh: 幼而聰慧，武帝愛之，恆在左右。
value.en: Wu Di doted on the bright boy and kept him always near.
value.literal: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.

value.zh: 嘗與諸皇子共戲殿上，惠帝來朝，執諸皇子手，次至太子，帝曰：「是汝兒也。」
value.en: Once he was playing on the palace steps with the imperial princes; when Emperor Hui came to audience, he took each prince's hand in turn; when he reached the crown prince, the emperor said, 'This is your son.'
value.literal: Once he was playing on the palace steps with the imperial princes; when Emperor Hui came to audience he took each prince's hand in turn; when he reached the crown prince, Emperor Wu said, 'This is your son.'

value.zh: 惠帝乃止。
value.en: Hui broke off his greeting.
value.literal: Emperor Hui thereupon stopped.

value.zh: 宮中嘗夜失火，武帝登樓望之。
value.en: A night blaze drew Wu Di to a high gallery.
value.literal: Once at night the palace caught fire; Emperor Wu climbed a tower to watch.

value.zh: 太子時年五歲，牽帝裾入暗中。
value.en: Five-year-old Yu pulled his grandfather into the dark.
value.literal: The crown prince was then five years old; he tugged the emperor's robe into the shadows.

value.zh: 帝問其故，太子曰：「暮夜倉卒，宜備非常，不宜令照見人君也。」
value.en: The crown prince said, "Suddenly at night one must guard against the unexpected; one must not let firelight reveal the ruler's face."
value.literal: The emperor asked why; the crown prince said, 'Suddenly at night one should guard against the unexpected; one must not let firelight reveal the ruler's face.'

value.zh: 由是奇之。
value.en: Wu Di marked him extraordinary.
value.literal: From this Wu Di marveled at him.

value.zh: 嘗從帝觀豕牢，言於帝曰：「豕甚肥，何不殺以享士，而使久費五穀？」
value.en: While watching the imperial sty he said to the emperor, "The pigs are very fat—why not slaughter them to feast the troops instead of letting them waste grain forever?"
value.literal: Once when following the emperor to view the pig pen he said to the emperor, 'The pigs are very fat—why not slaughter them to feast the troops instead of letting them waste grain forever?'

value.zh: 帝嘉其意，即使烹之。
value.en: Wu Di approved and had them slaughtered.
value.literal: The emperor praised his intent and at once ordered them cooked.

value.zh: 因撫其背，謂廷尉傅祗曰：「此兒當興我家。」
value.en: He stroked the boy's back and told Court Commandant Fu Zhi, "This child will bring prosperity to our house."
value.literal: He therefore stroked the boy's back and said to Court Commandant Fu Zhi, 'This child will bring prosperity to our house.'

value.zh: 嘗對群臣稱太子似宣帝，於是令譽流於天下。
value.en: He likened the heir to Sima Yi before court—reputation followed.
value.literal: He once declared before the assembled ministers that the crown prince resembled Emperor Xuan; thereafter praise of him spread through the realm.

value.zh: 及賈庶人死，乃誅劉振、孫慮、程據等，冊復太子曰：「皇帝使使持節、兼司空、衛尉伊策故皇太子之靈曰：嗚呼！
value.en: When Deposed Commoner Jia died, they executed Liu Zhen, Sun Lü, Cheng Ju, and others, and posthumously restored the crown prince; the edict read: "The emperor dispatches the credential-bearer, concurrent Director of Works, Commandant of the Guard Yi to announce by patent to the spirit of the late crown prince: Alas!
value.literal: When Deposed Commoner Jia died, they executed Liu Zhen, Sun Lü, Cheng Ju, and others, and posthumously restored the crown prince; the edict read: 'The emperor dispatches the credential-bearer, concurrent Director of Works, Commandant of the Guard Yi to announce by patent to the spirit of the late crown prince: Alas!

value.zh: 維爾少資岐嶷之質，荷先帝殊異之寵，大啟土宇，奄有淮陵。
value.en: In youth you were endowed with precocious wisdom and enjoyed the late emperor’s exceptional affection. He granted you a great domain and possession of Huailing.
value.literal: In youth you were endowed with precocious wisdom and enjoyed the late emperor’s exceptional affection. He granted you a great domain and possession of Huailing.

value.zh: 朕奉遵遺旨，越建爾儲副，以光顯我祖宗。
value.en: I followed his last wishes and established you as heir, to glorify our ancestors.
value.literal: I followed his last wishes and established you as heir, to glorify our ancestors.

value.zh: 祗爾德行，以從保傅，事親孝敬，禮無違者。
value.en: You were to revere virtuous conduct and follow your tutors, serve your parents with filial respect, and never violate ritual.
value.literal: I charged you to follow tutors in virtue, serving parents with filial respect—ritual unbreached.

value.zh: 而朕昧於凶構，致爾於非命之禍，俾申生、孝己復見於今。
value.en: Yet I failed to perceive wicked intrigues and brought you to an unnatural death, so that Shen Sheng and Xiao Ji appeared again in our time.
value.literal: Yet I, dim to vicious plots, brought you to the misfortune of untimely death, making Shen Sheng and Xiao Ji again appear in our day.

value.zh: 賴宰相賢明，人神憤怨，用啟朕心，討厥有罪，咸伏其辜。
value.en: Fortunately, wise ministers and the indignation of men and spirits opened my eyes; I punished the guilty, and all paid the penalty for their crimes.
value.literal: Thanks to wise ministers, human and spirit alike resented, opening my heart to punish the guilty—each has met sentence.

value.zh: 何補於荼毒冤魂酷痛哉？
value.en: But how can that make amends for the cruel suffering inflicted upon your wronged spirit?
value.literal: What use mending poisoned wronged souls' cruel pain?

value.zh: 是用忉怛悼恨，震動於五內。
value.en: Thus I grieve in anguish and regret, shaken to my innermost being.
value.literal: Therefore grief tears my vitals and shakes my five inner organs.

value.zh: 今追復皇太子喪禮，反葬京畿，祠乙太牢。
value.en: Now I restore the funeral rites due the crown prince, return your burial to the capital region, and offer a full tailao sacrifice of ox, sheep, and pig.
value.literal: Now I restore the funeral rites due the crown prince, return your burial to the capital region, and offer a full tailao sacrifice of ox, sheep, and pig.

value.zh: 魂而有靈，尚獲爾心。」
value.en: If soul possesses awareness may it receive this heart."
value.literal: If soul possesses awareness may it receive this heart.'

value.zh: 帝為太子服長子斬衰，群臣齊衰，使尚書和郁率東宮官屬具吉凶之制，迎太子喪于許昌。
value.en: Court mourned and fetched Yu's bier from Xu.
value.literal: The emperor wore unhemmed mourning for the crown prince as for an eldest son; the ministers wore hemmed mourning. He sent Minister He Yu to lead the Eastern Palace officials in preparing the prescribed auspicious and mourning rites and bringing the crown prince's bier back from Xuchang.

value.zh: 喪之發也，大風雷電，幃蓋飛裂。
value.en: Storm shattered funeral umbrellas.
value.literal: When the hearse set out great wind and thunder came—canopies and coverings flew torn.

value.zh: 又為哀策曰：「皇帝臨軒，使洗馬劉務告于皇太子之殯曰：咨爾遹！
value.en: They further composed a condolence text: "The emperor facing the gallery sends Groom of the Household Liu Wu to the crown prince's lying-in-state: Ah, Yu!
value.literal: They further composed a condolence text: 'The emperor facing the gallery sends Groom of the Household Liu Wu to the crown prince's lying-in-state: Ah, Yu!

value.zh: 幼稟英挺，芬馨誕茂。
value.en: From childhood you were outstanding, and your fine qualities flourished abundantly.
value.literal: You drew from youth heroic sap, fragrance ripe at birth.

value.zh: 既表髫齔，高明逸秀。
value.en: Even in early boyhood you displayed lofty brilliance and exceptional talents.
value.literal: Already in tied hair you stood lofty and bright.

value.zh: 昔爾聖祖，嘉爾淑美。
value.en: Your august grandfather cherished your fine virtues.
value.literal: Your holy ancestor prized your fine virtue.

value.zh: 顯詔仍崇，名振同軌。
value.en: Illustrious edicts repeatedly increased your honors; your fame resounded throughout the realm.
value.literal: Illustrious edicts repeatedly increased your honors; your fame resounded throughout the realm.

value.zh: 是用建爾儲副，永統皇基。
value.en: Therefore I established you as heir, to perpetuate the imperial foundations forever.
value.literal: Therefore I established you as heir, to perpetuate the imperial foundations forever.

value.zh: 如何凶戾潛構，禍害如茲！
value.en: How did vicious cruelty secretly weave harm like this!
value.literal: How did vicious cruelty secretly weave harm like this!

value.zh: 哀感和氣，痛貫四時。
value.en: Sorrow moves harmonious qi; pain pierces four seasons.
value.literal: Sorrow moves harmonious qi; pain pierces four seasons.

value.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！
value.en: Alas, how grievous!
value.literal: Alas, alas the sorrow!

value.zh: 爾之降廢，實我不明。
value.en: Your degradation was truly due to my lack of discernment.
value.literal: Your degradation was truly my blindness.

value.zh: 牝亂沈烖，釁結禍成。
value.en: A woman’s disorder brought deep calamity; hostility accumulated and disaster took shape.
value.literal: Female chaos sank calamity; omens knotted into disaster.

value.zh: 爾之逝矣，誰百其形？
value.en: Now that you have departed, who could offer a hundredfold ransom for your person?
value.literal: Now that you have departed, who could offer a hundredfold ransom for your person?

value.zh: 昔之申生，含枉莫訟。
value.en: Long ago Shen Sheng bore false charges, with none to plead his case.
value.literal: Long ago Shen Sheng bore wrong yet could not plead.

value.zh: 今爾之負，抱冤於東。
value.en: Now you too bear unjust blame and nurse your grievance in the east.
value.literal: Now your burden of grievance hugs the eastern lands.

value.zh: 悠悠有識，孰不哀慟！
value.en: Among all who understand, who would not grieve?
value.literal: Far and near anyone with insight—who fails bitter grief!

value.zh: 壺關幹主，千秋悟己。
value.en: The elder of Huguan remonstrated with his ruler; Qianqiu brought him to recognize his error.
value.literal: The elder of Huguan remonstrated with his ruler; Qianqiu brought him to recognize his error.

value.zh: 異世同規，古今一理。
value.en: Across different ages, the pattern is the same; past and present share one principle.
value.literal: Different age, same rule—past and present one principle.

value.zh: 皇孫啟建，隆祚爾子。
value.en: Your son has been established as imperial grandson-heir, continuing the dynastic blessing through him.
value.literal: Your son has been established as imperial grandson-heir, continuing the dynastic blessing through him.

value.zh: 雖悴前終，庶榮後始。
value.en: Though your own end was sorrowful, may the new beginning afterward be glorious.
value.literal: Though front end withered, rear blossom may yet flourish.

value.zh: 窀穸既營，將寧爾神。
value.en: Your burial chamber is now prepared, to bring your spirit peace.
value.literal: Burial vault now built—we pacify your spirit.

value.zh: 華髦電逝，戎車雷震。
value.en: Splendid plumes flash past like lightning; war chariots rumble like thunder.
value.literal: Flower feathers flash like lightning; war wagons thunder.

value.zh: 芒芒羽蓋，翼翼縉紳。
value.en: Feathered canopies stretch far and wide; the gentry advance in orderly ranks.
value.literal: Vast feather-canopies; crowded sash-and-hat ranks.

value.zh: 同悲等痛，孰不酸辛！
value.en: Courtiers weep together.
value.literal: Shared grief and equal pain—who lacks bitter sorrow!

value.zh: 庶光來葉，永世不泯。」
value.en: May light reach posterity, never extinguished through ages."
value.literal: May light reach posterity, never extinguished through ages.'

value.zh: 諡曰湣懷。
value.en: Canonized Crown Prince Minhuai.
value.literal: Posthumous title Minhuai was granted.

value.zh: 六月己卯，葬于顯平陵。
value.en: Buried sixth month at Xianping.
value.literal: On jimao day of the sixth month he was buried at Xianping Mausoleum.

value.zh: 帝感閻纘之言，立思子台，故臣江統、陸機並作誄頌焉。
value.en: Yan Zuan's plea built Son-Lament Terrace—Jiang Tong and Lu Ji wrote elegies.
value.literal: Moved by Yan Zuan's words the emperor raised a Terrace of Longing for Sons; former ministers Jiang Tong and Lu Ji both composed dirges.

value.zh: 太子三子：虨、臧、尚，並與父同幽金墉。
value.en: Three sons shared Yu's prison.
value.literal: The crown prince had three sons—Bin, Zang, and Shang—all imprisoned with their father at Jinyong.

value.zh: 史臣曰：湣懷挺岐嶷之姿，表夙成之質。
value.en: The historiographers say: Minhuai was endowed with exceptional wisdom and displayed precocious gifts.
value.literal: The historiographers say: Minhuai bore a posture keen and wise, displaying precocious substance.

value.zh: 武皇鍾愛，既深詒厥之謀；
value.en: Wu Di planned Yu as future pillar.
value.literal: Emperor Wu cherished him and deeply laid succession plans.

value.zh: 天下歸心，頗有後來之望。
value.en: The realm expected greatness.
value.literal: All under Heaven turned hearts toward him—high hopes attended his future.

value.zh: 及於繼明宸極，守器春坊，四教不勤，三朝或闕，豹姿未變，鳳德已衰，信惑奸邪，疏斥正士，好屠酤之賤役，耽苑囿之佚遊，可謂靡不有初，鮮克有終者也。
value.en: When the new ruler ascended the imperial throne and the prince guarded the succession in the Eastern Palace, he neglected the four teachings and sometimes omitted the three daily greetings. His leopard’s form was not yet transformed, while his phoenix virtue had already declined. He trusted wicked deceivers and drove away upright men, enjoyed the lowly work of butchering and selling wine, and indulged in idle outings in the parks. Truly one may say: "All have a beginning, but few carry through to the end."
value.literal: When the new ruler ascended the imperial throne and the prince guarded the succession in the Eastern Palace, he neglected the four teachings and sometimes omitted the three daily greetings. His leopard’s form was not yet transformed, while his phoenix virtue had already declined. He trusted wicked deceivers and drove away upright men, enjoyed the lowly work of butchering and selling wine, and indulged in idle outings in the parks. Truly one may say: "All have a beginning, but few carry through to the end."

value.zh: 既而中宮凶忍，久懷危害之心，外戚諂諛，競進讒邪之說；
value.en: Thereupon the inner palace proved fierce and cruel, long harboring murderous intent; outer kin flattered, competing to advance slander.
value.literal: Thereupon the inner palace proved fierce and cruel, long harboring murderous intent; outer kin flattered, competing to advance slander.

value.zh: 坎牲之謀已構，斃犬之譖遂行；
value.en: The plot involving a sacrificial victim had already been laid; the slander involving a dead dog then took effect.
value.literal: The plot involving a sacrificial victim had already been laid; the slander involving a dead dog then took effect.

value.zh: 一人乏探隱之聰，百辟無爭臣之節。
value.en: The ruler lacked the discernment to uncover hidden matters, and the ministers lacked the integrity to remonstrate.
value.literal: Thus one man lacked keen insight into hidden matters; the hundred ministers showed no temper of remonstrating subjects.

value.zh: 遂使冤逾楚建，酷甚戾園。
value.en: Thus the injustice exceeded that done to Jian of Chu, and the cruelty surpassed the tragedy commemorated at Li Garden.
value.literal: Thus the injustice exceeded that done to Jian of Chu, and the cruelty surpassed the tragedy commemorated at Li Garden.

value.zh: 雖復禮備哀榮，情深憫慟，亦何補於荼毒者哉！
value.en: Posthumous honors could not resurrect him.
value.literal: Though mourning rites ran full and grief ran deep, what did they mend for the poisoned innocent!

value.zh: 贊曰：湣懷聰穎，諒惟天挺。
value.en: The encomium says: Minhuai was intelligent and perceptive, truly endowed by Heaven.
value.literal: The encomium says: Minhuai clever and keen—truly Heaven-endowed.

value.zh: 皇祖鐘心，庶僚引領。
value.en: His imperial grandfather cherished him deeply; the assembled officials looked forward in expectation.
value.literal: Imperial ancestor pinned hope on him; hosts of officials craned necks.

value.zh: 震宮肇建，儲德不恢。
value.en: When he first entered the heir’s palace, his princely virtue failed to grow.
value.literal: When Thunder Palace first rose, heir virtue never broadened.

value.zh: 掇蜂構隙，歸胙生災。
value.en: Gathering wasps opened a breach; sending back sacrificial meat brought disaster.
value.literal: Gathering wasps opened a breach; sending back sacrificial meat brought disaster.

value.zh: 既罹凶忍，徒望歸來。
value.en: Death ended every hope of restoration.
value.literal: Once brutal cruelty struck, vain hope alone remained of return.

value.zh: 褚遂良 韓瑗 來濟 上官儀
value.en: Chu Suiliang, Han Yuan, Lai Ji, and Shang Guanyi
value.literal: Chu Suiliang, Han Yuan, Lai Ji, Shang Guanyi

value.zh: 褚遂良，散騎常侍亮之子也。
value.en: Chu Suiliang was the son of Chu Liang, who had served as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
value.literal: Chu Suiliang was the son of the Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Chu Liang.

value.zh: 太業末，隨父在隴右，薛舉僭號，署為通事舍人。
value.en: In the final years of the Sui Daye era, he accompanied his father to Longyou. When Xue Ju declared himself ruler, he appointed Chu Suiliang Master of Communications.
value.literal: At the end of the Daye reign, he followed his father to Longyou; Xue Ju usurped a title and appointed him Master of Communications.

value.zh: 舉敗歸國，授秦州都督府鎧曹參軍。
value.en: After Xue Ju's defeat, he submitted to the Tang and was appointed aide in the Armor Section of the Qinzhou Area Command headquarters.
value.literal: When Ju was defeated he returned to the state and was granted the post of Army Armor Section aide in the Qinzhou Area Command.

value.zh: 貞觀十年，自秘書郎遷起居郎。
value.en: In 636, he was promoted from Secretary to Attendant of the Bedchamber.
value.literal: In the tenth year of Zhenguan, he moved from Secretary to Attendant of the Bedchamber.

value.zh: 遂良博涉文史，尤工隸書，父友歐陽詢甚重之。
value.en: Suiliang was widely read in literature and history and was especially accomplished in clerical script. Ouyang Xun, a friend of his father, held him in high regard.
value.literal: Suiliang was broadly versed in literature and history and especially skilled in clerical script; his father's friend Ouyang Xun greatly valued him.

value.zh: 太宗嘗謂侍中魏徵曰：「虞世南死後，無人可以論書。」
value.en: Emperor Taizong once told Palace Attendant Wei Zheng, "Since Yu Shinan died, I have had no one with whom to discuss calligraphy."
value.literal: The Taizong Emperor once said to the Palace Attendant Wei Zheng: "After Yu Shinan died, there is no one with whom to discuss calligraphy."

value.zh: 徵曰：「褚遂良下筆遒勁，甚得王逸少體。」
value.en: Wei Zheng replied, "Chu Suiliang's brushwork is vigorous and powerful, and it captures Wang Xizhi's style remarkably well."
value.literal: Zheng said: "Chu Suiliang's brushwork is forceful and vigorous and very much captures Wang Yishao's style."

value.zh: 太宗即日召令侍書。
value.en: That same day, Taizong summoned him to serve at court as a calligrapher.
value.literal: That same day the Taizong Emperor summoned him and ordered him to attend at writing.

value.zh: 太宗嘗出御府金帛購求王羲之書跡，天下爭齎古書詣闕以獻，當時莫能辯其真偽，遂良備論所出，一無舛誤。
value.en: Taizong once used gold and silk from the imperial treasury to buy works attributed to Wang Xizhi. People across the empire rushed ancient books to court as offerings, and at the time no one could tell which were genuine. Suiliang identified the provenance of each piece without a single mistake.
value.literal: The Taizong Emperor once issued gold and silk from the imperial treasury to purchase traces of Wang Xizhi's writing; all under Heaven vied to bring ancient books to the palace to present, and at the time none could distinguish true from false—Suiliang discussed in full their provenance, without a single error.

value.zh: 十五年，詔有事太山，先幸洛陽，有星孛於太微，犯郎位。
value.en: In 641, an edict ordered rites at Mount Tai. The emperor first visited Luoyang, where a comet appeared in the Supreme Palace Enclosure constellation and trespassed upon the Retinue stars.
value.literal: In the fifteenth year, an edict ordered rites at Mount Tai; first he visited Luoyang; a broom star appeared in the Supreme Palace Enclosure and encroached on the Retinue positions.

value.zh: 遂良言於太宗曰：「陛下撥亂反正，功超前烈，將告成東嶽，天下幸甚。
value.en: Suiliang said to Taizong, "Your Majesty quelled chaos and restored order, and your achievements surpass those of former sages. You are about to complete the rites at the Eastern Peak, to the great fortune of the realm.
value.literal: Suiliang spoke to the Taizong Emperor, saying: "Your Majesty has quelled disorder and restored the right, your achievements surpassing former worthies; you are about to announce completion at the Eastern Peak—the realm is greatly fortunate.

value.zh: 而行至洛陽，彗星輒見，此或有所未允合者也。
value.en: Yet upon reaching Luoyang, a comet appeared at once. This may mean that something is not yet in accord with Heaven's will.
value.literal: Yet upon reaching Luoyang the comet promptly appeared—this perhaps indicates something not yet in accord.

value.zh: 且漢武優柔數年，始行岱禮，臣愚伏願詳擇。」
value.en: Moreover, Emperor Wu of Han deliberated for years before he finally performed the rites at Mount Tai. In my humble view, I beg Your Majesty to choose the timing with great care."
value.literal: Moreover Emperor Wu of Han hesitated for several years before performing the Dai rites; this subject in his folly prostrates himself wishing Your Majesty to deliberate carefully."

value.zh: 太宗深然之，下詔罷封禪之事。
value.en: Taizong strongly agreed and issued an edict canceling the feng and shan ceremonies.
value.literal: The Taizong Emperor deeply approved this and issued an edict halting the feng and shan affairs.

value.zh: 其年，遷諫議大夫，兼知起居事。
value.en: That year he was promoted to Grand Master of Remonstrance and was also put in charge of the bedchamber records.
value.literal: That year he was transferred to Grand Master of Remonstrance and concurrently managed bedchamber affairs.

value.zh: 太宗嘗問：「卿知起居，記錄何事，大抵人君得觀之否？」
value.en: Taizong once asked, "As keeper of the bedchamber records, what do you write down? May a ruler generally read them?"
value.literal: The Taizong Emperor once asked: "You manage the bedchamber records—what affairs do you record? Can a ruler in general view them?"

value.zh: 遂良對曰：「今之起居，古左右史，書人君言事，且記善惡，以為鑑誡，庶幾人主不為非法。
value.en: Suiliang answered, "The bedchamber records of today are the ancient Left and Right Historians. They record the ruler's words and deeds, noting good and evil alike, so that they may serve as a mirror and a warning and keep the sovereign from unlawful acts.
value.literal: Suiliang replied: "Today's bedchamber records are the ancient Left and Right Historians; they write the ruler's words and affairs, and also record good and evil, to serve as mirror and warning, so that perhaps the sovereign will not do what is unlawful.

value.zh: 不聞帝王躬自觀史。」
value.en: I have never heard of an emperor reading his own history himself."
value.literal: One does not hear of emperors and kings personally viewing the histories."

value.zh: 太宗曰：「朕有不善，卿必記之耶？」
value.en: Taizong said, "If I do something wrong, will you record that too?"
value.literal: The Taizong Emperor said: "If I have what is not good, will you surely record it?"

value.zh: 遂良曰：「守道不如守官，臣職當載筆，君舉必記。」
value.en: Suiliang said, "Upholding moral principle is less binding than upholding one's office. My duty is to hold the brush: whatever Your Majesty does, I must record it."
value.literal: Suiliang said: "Keeping the Way is not as good as keeping one's office; this subject's duty is to bear the brush—whatever the ruler does must be recorded."

value.zh: 黃門侍郎劉洎曰：「設令遂良不記，天下亦記之矣。」
value.en: Yellow Gate Attendant Liu Ji said, "Even if Suiliang did not record it, the realm would still record it."
value.literal: Yellow Gate Attendant Liu Ji said: "Suppose Suiliang did not record it—the realm would still record it."

value.zh: 太宗以為然。
value.en: Taizong agreed that this was so.
value.literal: The Taizong Emperor considered this correct.

value.zh: 時魏王為太宗所愛，禮秩如嫡。
value.en: At that time the Prince of Wei was a favorite of Taizong, and his ceremonial standing was treated like that of the legitimate heir.
value.literal: At the time the Prince of Wei was loved by the Taizong Emperor, his ritual rank like that of the legitimate heir.

value.zh: 其年，太宗問侍臣曰：「當今國家何事最急？」
value.en: That year Taizong asked his ministers, "What is the most urgent matter facing the state today?"
value.literal: That year the Taizong Emperor asked his attending ministers: "In the state today, what matter is most urgent?"

value.zh: 中書侍郎岑文本曰：「《傳》稱『導之以德，齊之以禮』，由斯而言。
value.en: Central Secretariat Attendant Cen Wende said, "The Analects say, 'Lead them with virtue and harmonize them with ritual.' From that perspective—
value.literal: Central Secretariat Attendant Cen Wende said: "The Documents say 'Lead them with virtue, regulate them with ritual'—speaking from this.

value.zh: 禮義為急。」
value.en: ritual and righteousness are the most urgent matters."
value.literal: Ritual and righteousness are urgent."

value.zh: 遂良進曰：「當今四方仰德，誰敢為非？
value.en: Suiliang stepped forward and said, "Today the four quarters look up to Your Majesty's virtue. Who would dare do wrong?
value.literal: Suiliang advanced and said: "Today the four quarters look up to virtue—who would dare do wrong?

value.zh: 但太子、諸王，須有定分，陛下宜為萬代法以遺子孫。」
value.en: But the Crown Prince and the other princes must have fixed ranks and roles. Your Majesty should establish a precedent for ten thousand generations to pass on to your descendants."
value.literal: But the Crown Prince and the various princes must have fixed distinctions; Your Majesty should make a law for ten thousand generations to bequeath to descendants."

value.zh: 太宗曰：「此言是也。
value.en: Taizong said, "That is true.
value.literal: The Taizong Emperor said: "This statement is correct.

value.zh: 朕年將五十，已覺衰怠。
value.en: I am nearly fifty and already feel my strength failing.
value.literal: I am nearing fifty years and already feel decline and weariness.

value.zh: 既以長子守器東宮，弟及庶子數將五十，心常憂慮，頗在此耳。
value.en: I have already installed my eldest son as heir in the Eastern Palace, but I have nearly fifty younger sons and sons by concubines. What weighs on my mind most is precisely this.
value.literal: Having already installed the eldest son to guard the vessel in the Eastern Palace, younger brothers and sons by concubines number nearly fifty—I constantly worry in my heart, and it lies largely in this.

value.zh: 但自古嫡庶無良佐，何嘗不傾敗國家？
value.en: Yet since antiquity, when legitimate and illegitimate lines lacked good advisers, when did they not bring ruin upon a state?
value.literal: Yet since antiquity legitimate and illegitimate lines without good assistants—when have they not overturned and ruined states?

value.zh: 公等為朕搜訪賢德，以傅儲宮，爰及諸王，咸求正士。
value.en: Search out worthy men for me to tutor the Heir Apparent, and find upright men for all the princes as well.
value.literal: You gentlemen should for me search out the worthy and virtuous to tutor the Heir Apparent, and extending to the various princes, all seek upright men.

value.zh: 且事人歲久，即分義情深，非意窺窬，多由此作。」
value.en: Moreover, when men serve a prince for many years, their bond of loyalty grows deep. Unintended ambitions for the throne often arise from just such circumstances."
value.literal: Moreover, serving a person for many years, then the bond of duty grows deep—unintended coveting of the throne often arises from this."

value.zh: 於是限王府官僚不得過四考。
value.en: Thereupon he limited officials in princely establishments to no more than four terms of service.
value.literal: Thereupon he limited princely establishment officials to no more than four performance reviews.

value.zh: 十七年，太宗問遂良曰：「舜造漆器，禹雕其俎，當時諫舜、禹者十餘人。
value.en: In 643, Taizong asked Suiliang, "Shun made lacquer vessels, and Yu carved his sacrificial stands. More than ten men remonstrated with them at the time.
value.literal: In the seventeenth year the Taizong Emperor asked Suiliang: "Shun made lacquer vessels; Yu carved his sacrificial stands—at the time more than ten persons remonstrated with Shun and Yu.

value.zh: 食器之間，苦諫何也？」
value.en: Why such strenuous remonstrance over mere eating vessels?"
value.literal: Among eating vessels, why such strenuous remonstrance?"

value.zh: 遂良對曰：「雕琢害農事，纂組傷女工。
value.en: Suiliang answered, "Carving and polishing harm farming, and brocade work injures women's labor.
value.literal: Suiliang replied: "Carving and polishing harm agricultural affairs; brocade and embroidery injure women's work.

value.zh: 首創奢淫，危亡之漸。
value.en: To be the first to indulge in luxury is the first step on the road to ruin.
value.literal: First creating extravagance and dissipation is the gradual approach of peril and ruin.

value.zh: 漆器不已，必金為之；
value.en: If lacquer vessels are not enough, one will make them of gold;
value.literal: If lacquer vessels do not stop, they must be made of gold;

value.zh: 金器不已，必玉為之。
value.en: and if gold is not enough, one will make them of jade.
value.literal: if gold vessels do not stop, they must be made of jade.

value.zh: 所以諍臣必諫其漸，及其滿盈，無所復諫。」
value.en: That is why remonstrating ministers must speak at the first sign of excess. Once luxury has overflowed, there is nothing left to remonstrate about."
value.literal: Therefore remonstrating ministers must remonstrate at the gradual stage; when it reaches fullness and overflow, there is nothing further to remonstrate about."

value.zh: 太宗以為然，因曰：「夫為人君，不憂萬姓而事奢淫，危亡之機可反掌而待也。」
value.en: Taizong agreed and added, "For a ruler of men, to neglect the welfare of the people and pursue luxury instead is to invite ruin with a turn of the hand."
value.literal: The Taizong Emperor considered this correct and then said: "For one who is ruler of men, not to worry for the myriad people but to pursue extravagance and dissipation—the moment of peril and ruin can be awaited with a turn of the palm."

value.zh: 時皇子年幼者多任都督、刺史，遂良上疏曰：「昔兩漢以郡國理人，除郡以外，分立諸子。
value.en: At that time many young princes were appointed as area commanders and prefects. Suiliang submitted a memorial: "In the two Han dynasties, the realm was governed through commanderies and kingdoms. Apart from the commanderies, the emperor's sons were granted separate domains.
value.literal: At the time many young princes were appointed area commanders and prefects; Suiliang submitted a memorial saying: "Formerly the two Han used commanderies and kingdoms to govern people; apart from commanderies they separately established the various sons.

value.zh: 割土分疆，雜用周制。
value.en: They divided territory and apportioned domains, mixing in institutions from the Zhou.
value.literal: Dividing territory and apportioning borders, they mixed in Zhou institutions.

value.zh: 皇唐州縣，祖依秦法。
value.en: Great Tang's prefectures and counties follow the Qin model as their foundation.
value.literal: Great Tang's prefectures and counties follow the Qin law as ancestor.

value.zh: 皇子幼年，或授刺史，陛下豈不以王之骨肉，鎮扞四方？
value.en: When princes are still young, some are made prefects. Does Your Majesty not intend your own flesh and blood to guard the four quarters?
value.literal: When princes are young, some are granted prefectures—is not Your Majesty using the king's flesh and bone to guard and defend the four quarters?

value.zh: 此之造制，道高前烈。
value.en: In creating this system, Your Majesty's principle surpasses that of former sages.
value.literal: This institution surpasses former worthies in principle.

value.zh: 如臣愚見，有小未盡。
value.en: In my humble view, however, one small matter remains incomplete.
value.literal: In this subject's foolish view, there is something small not yet complete.

value.zh: 何者？
value.en: What is it?
value.literal: What is it?

value.zh: 刺史郡帥，民仰以安。
value.en: A prefect is the commander of a commandery, and the people depend on him for their security.
value.literal: Prefects are commanders of commanderies; the people look up to them for security.

value.zh: 得一善人，部內蘇息；
value.en: With one good man in office, the district revives;
value.literal: Obtain one good man and the district revives;

value.zh: 遇一不善，合州勞弊。
value.en: but with one bad man, the whole prefecture is worn down and exhausted.
value.literal: meet one who is not good and the whole prefecture is worn and exhausted.

value.zh: 是以人君愛恤百姓，常為擇賢。
value.en: That is why a ruler who loves his people constantly selects worthy men for office.
value.literal: Therefore the ruler of men loves and cherishes the hundred names and constantly selects the worthy for them.

value.zh: 或稱河潤九里，京師蒙福；
value.en: Some say that when a river nourishes the land for nine li, the capital shares in the blessing;
value.literal: Some say the river moistens for nine li and the capital receives blessing;

value.zh: 或人興歌詠，生為立祠。
value.en: or the people sing his praises and build shrines to him while he still lives.
value.literal: or the people rise in song and praise and while living build shrines for him.

value.zh: 漢宣帝云：『與我共理者，惟良二千石。』
value.en: Emperor Xuan of Han said, 'Those who govern with me are only good prefects.'
value.literal: Emperor Xuan of Han said: 'Those who govern with me are only good two-thousand-dan officials.'

value.zh: 如臣愚見，陛下兒子內年齒尚幼、未堪臨人者，且留京師，教以經學。
value.en: In my humble view, among Your Majesty's sons, those who are still too young to govern people should remain in the capital for now and be taught the classics.
value.literal: In this subject's foolish view, among Your Majesty's sons those whose years are still young and not yet able to oversee people should for the present remain in the capital and be taught the classics.

value.zh: 一則畏天之威，不敢犯禁；
value.en: First, they will fear Heaven's majesty and not dare break the law;
value.literal: First, they will fear Heaven's majesty and not dare violate prohibitions;

value.zh: 二則觀見朝儀，自然成立。
value.en: second, they will observe court ritual and naturally learn how to conduct themselves.
value.literal: second, they will observe and see court ritual and naturally be formed.

value.zh: 因此積習，自知為人。
value.en: Through such accumulated habit, they will learn on their own how to be men.
value.literal: Through this accumulated practice they will themselves know how to be human.

value.zh: 審堪臨州，然後遣出。
value.en: Only when they are truly fit to govern a prefecture should they be sent out.
value.literal: When it is verified that they can oversee a prefecture, then send them out.

value.zh: 臣謹按漢明、章、和三帝，能友愛於弟，自茲已降，取為準的。
value.en: I respectfully note that Emperors Ming, Zhang, and He of Han were able to treat their younger brothers with affection. Let us take them as our standard from this point forward.
value.literal: This subject respectfully notes that the Ming, Zhang, and He emperors of Han were able to be friendly and loving toward their younger brothers; from this down, take them as the standard.

value.zh: 封立諸王，雖各有國土，年尚幼小者，召留京師，訓以禮法，垂以恩惠。
value.en: When they enfeoffed the various kings, each received his own domain, but those who were still young were summoned to remain in the capital, instructed in ritual and law, and showered with favor.
value.literal: Enfeoffing and establishing the various kings, although each had his own territory, those whose years were still young were summoned to remain in the capital, instructed in ritual and law, and bestowed with favor.

value.zh: 訖三帝世，諸王數十百人，唯二王稍惡，自余餐和染教，皆為善人。
value.en: Through the reigns of those three emperors, the princes numbered in the tens and hundreds. Only two princes turned out badly; the rest, nourished by harmony and shaped by instruction, all became good men.
value.literal: Through the three emperors' reigns, the various kings numbered in the tens and hundreds—only two kings were somewhat bad; the rest, nourished by harmony and dyed by instruction, all became good men.

value.zh: 則前事已驗，惟陛下詳察。」
value.en: The precedent has already been tested. I beg Your Majesty to consider it carefully."
value.literal: Then former affairs have already been verified—only may Your Majesty examine carefully."

value.zh: 太宗深納之。
value.en: Taizong accepted this advice wholeheartedly.
value.literal: The Taizong Emperor deeply accepted this.

value.zh: 其年，太子承乾以罪廢，魏王泰入侍，太宗面許立為太子。
value.en: That year Crown Prince Chengqian was deposed for his crimes. The Prince of Wei, Li Tai, attended the emperor in person, and Taizong openly promised to make him crown prince.
value.literal: That year the Crown Prince Chengqian was deposed for crime; the Prince of Wei Tai entered attendance; the Taizong Emperor to his face promised to establish him as Crown Prince.

value.zh: 因謂侍臣曰：「昨青雀自投我懷云：『臣今日始得與陛下為子，更生之日也。
value.en: He then told his ministers, "Yesterday the Green Sparrow threw himself into my arms and said, 'Today I have at last become Your Majesty's son in truth. It is like being born again.
value.literal: He then said to his attending ministers: "Yesterday the Green Sparrow threw himself into my embrace, saying: 'Your subject today for the first time obtains to be a son with Your Majesty—it is a day of rebirth.

value.zh: 臣唯有一子，臣百年之後，當為陛下殺之，傳國晉王。』
value.en: I have only one son. After I die, I will kill him for Your Majesty's sake and pass the realm to the Prince of Jin.
value.literal: Your subject has only one son; after Your subject's hundred years I shall for Your Majesty kill him and pass the state to the Prince of Jin.

value.zh: 父子之道，故當天性，我見其如此，甚憐之。」
value.en: The bond between father and son is a matter of nature. When I saw him speak so, I was deeply moved.'"
value.literal: The way of father and son ought by nature to be thus—I saw him like this and greatly pitied him.'"

value.zh: 遂良進曰：「陛下失言。
value.en: Suiliang stepped forward and said, "Your Majesty has spoken unwisely.
value.literal: Suiliang advanced and said: "Your Majesty has misspoken.

value.zh: 伏願審思，無令錯誤也。
value.en: I beg Your Majesty to think this through carefully and not make a mistake.
value.literal: I prostrate myself wishing Your Majesty to deliberate carefully and not let there be error.

value.zh: 安有陛下百年之後，魏王執權為天下之主，而能殺其愛子，傳國於晉王者乎？
value.en: After Your Majesty is gone, when the Prince of Wei holds power as ruler of the realm, would he truly kill his own beloved son and pass the throne to the Prince of Jin?
value.literal: How could there be, after Your Majesty's hundred years, the Prince of Wei holding power as lord of all under Heaven yet able to kill his beloved son and pass the state to the Prince of Jin?

value.zh: 陛下昔立承乾為太子，而復寵愛魏王，禮數或有逾於承乾者，良由嫡庶不分，所以至此。
value.en: Your Majesty once made Chengqian crown prince, yet continued to favor the Prince of Wei, sometimes treating him with honors that exceeded Chengqian's. This came about because legitimate and illegitimate lines were not kept distinct.
value.literal: Your Majesty formerly established Chengqian as Crown Prince, yet again showed favor to the Prince of Wei, ritual count sometimes exceeding Chengqian's—truly because legitimate and illegitimate were not distinguished, therefore it came to this.

value.zh: 殷鑑不遠，足為龜鏡。
value.en: The lesson of the recent past is close at hand and should serve as a mirror for Your Majesty.
value.literal: The Yin mirror is not far—sufficient to serve as tortoise mirror.

value.zh: 陛下今日既立魏王，伏願陛下別安置晉王，始得安全耳。」
value.en: Now that Your Majesty has chosen the Prince of Wei, I beg Your Majesty to make separate arrangements for the Prince of Jin. Only then will he be safe."
value.literal: Your Majesty today having already established the Prince of Wei, I prostrate myself wishing Your Majesty to separately settle the Prince of Jin—only then can there be security."

value.zh: 太宗涕泗交下曰：「我不能。」
value.en: Taizong wept openly and said, "I cannot do that."
value.literal: The Taizong Emperor, tears and mucus crossing his face, said: "I cannot."

value.zh: 即日召長孫無忌、房玄齡、李勣與遂良等定策，立晉王為皇太子。
value.en: That same day he summoned Zhangsun Wuji, Fang Xuanling, Li Ji, Suiliang, and others to settle the succession and install the Prince of Jin as crown prince.
value.literal: That same day he summoned Zhangsun Wuji, Fang Xuanling, Li Ji, and Suiliang and others to fix the policy and establish the Prince of Jin as Crown Prince.

value.zh: 時頻有飛雉集於宮殿之內，太宗問群臣曰：「是何祥也？」
value.en: At that time wild pheasants were frequently seen gathering inside the palace. Taizong asked his ministers, "What omen does this signify?"
value.literal: At the time pheasants frequently gathered within the palace halls; the Taizong Emperor asked his ministers: "What omen is this?"

value.zh: 對曰：「昔秦文公時，有童子化為雉，雌者鳴於陳倉，雄者鳴於南陽。
value.en: They answered, "In the time of Duke Wen of Qin, a boy transformed into a pheasant. The female cried at Chencang, and the male cried at Nanyang.
value.literal: They replied: "Formerly in the time of Duke Wen of Qin, a boy transformed into a pheasant; the female cried at Chencang, the male cried at Nanyang.

value.zh: 童子曰：得雄者王，得雌者霸。
value.en: The boy said, 'He who obtains the male will become king; he who obtains the female will become hegemon.'
value.literal: The boy said: He who obtains the male will be king; he who obtains the female will be hegemon.

value.zh: 文公遂以為寶雞。
value.en: Duke Wen thereupon took it as an auspicious sign from Chen.
value.literal: Duke Wen thereupon took it as the treasured cock of Chen.

value.zh: 後漢光武得雄，遂起南陽而有四海。
value.en: Later, Emperor Guangwu of Han obtained the male pheasant, rose from Nanyang, and won the realm.
value.literal: Later Emperor Guangwu of Han obtained the male and thereupon rose from Nanyang to possess the four seas.

value.zh: 陛下舊封秦王，故雄雉見於秦地，此所以彰表明德也。」
value.en: Your Majesty was once enfeoffed as Prince of Qin, so the male pheasant has appeared in Qin territory. This is a sign that your bright virtue is being made manifest."
value.literal: Your Majesty was formerly enfeoffed as Prince of Qin, therefore the male pheasant appeared in Qin territory—this is how bright virtue is made manifest."

value.zh: 太宗悅曰：「立身之道，不可無學，遂良博識，深可重也。」
value.en: Taizong said with pleasure, "The way to establish oneself in the world cannot be learned without study. Suiliang is deeply learned and truly worthy of respect."
value.literal: The Taizong Emperor, pleased, said: "The Way of establishing oneself cannot be without learning—Suiliang is broadly knowledgeable and deeply to be valued."

value.zh: 尋授太子賓客。
value.en: Soon afterward he was appointed Guest of the Crown Prince.
value.literal: Shortly he was appointed Guest of the Crown Prince.

value.zh: 豆盧革，祖籍，同州刺史。
value.en: Dou Luge's grandfather Ji served as prefect of Tongzhou.
value.literal: Dou Luge; ancestral register; Tongzhou prefect.

value.zh: 父瓚，舒州刺史。
value.en: His father Zan was prefect of Shuzhou.
value.literal: His father Zan was prefect of Shu.

value.zh: 〈（《宣和書譜》云：失其世係。）〉
value.en: (The Xuanhe Calligraphy Catalogue notes that his pedigree is lost.)〉
value.literal: (The Xuanhe Calligraphy Catalogue states: his genealogical line is lost.)〉

value.zh: 革少值亂離，避地鄜、延，轉入中山，王處直禮之，辟於幕下，有奏記之譽。
value.en: In his youth Ge lived through war and exile, taking refuge in Fu and Yan before moving on to Zhongshan. Wang Chuzhi honored him and brought him onto his staff, where he gained a reputation for polished memorials and dispatches.
value.literal: Ge in youth encountered turmoil and dispersal, fled to Fu and Yan, then moved into Zhongshan; Wang Chuzhi treated him with courtesy and recruited him to his staff, where he won renown for memorials and letters.

value.zh: 因牡丹會賦詩，諷處直以桑柘為意，言甚古雅，漸加器仰，轉節度判官。
value.en: At a peony festival he wrote a poem that, through mulberry and ramie, gently admonished Chuzhi. The verse was so refined and archaic in tone that Chuzhi came to esteem him ever more highly and promoted him to adjutant of the military commission.
value.literal: At a peony gathering he composed a poem, admonishing Chuzhi with mulberry and ramie as his theme; his language was very antique and elegant, and Chuzhi came increasingly to esteem him, promoting him to military commissioner adjutant.

value.zh: 而理家無法，獨請謁處直，處直慮布政有缺，有所規諫，斂版出迎，乃為嬖人祈軍職矣。
value.en: Yet he ran his household without discipline. When he alone sought an audience with Chuzhi, the lord, worried that his own governance might be at fault, came to remonstrate with him. Ge put away his tablet and came out to receive him — only to ask a military appointment for a favorite.
value.literal: Yet in managing his household he had no discipline; he alone requested audience with Chuzhi. Chuzhi, fearing a gap in his governance, went to remonstrate; Ge folded his tablet and came out to meet him — only to beg a military post for a favorite.

value.zh: 任圜，京兆三原人。
value.en: Ren Huan was a native of Sanyuan in Jingzhao.
value.literal: Ren Huan, a native of Sanyuan in Jingzhao.

value.zh: 祖清，成都少尹。
value.en: His grandfather Qing served as vice governor of Chengdu.
value.literal: His grandfather Qing was vice governor of Chengdu.

value.zh: 父茂宏，避地太原，奏授西河令；
value.en: His father Maohong fled the turmoil to Taiyuan, where he was appointed by memorial as magistrate of Xihe.
value.literal: His father Maohong, fleeing disorder, reached Taiyuan and was appointed by memorial as magistrate of Xihe;

value.zh: 有子五人，曰圖、回、圜、團、冏，風彩俱異。
value.en: He had five sons — Tu, Hui, Huan, Tuan, and Jiong — each with a striking bearing.
value.literal: He had five sons, named Tu, Hui, Huan, Tuan, and Jiong — each with striking presence.

value.zh: 武皇愛之，以宗女妻團，歷代、憲二郡刺史。
value.en: Emperor Wu favored the family and married an imperial clanswoman to Tuan, who served successively as prefect of Dai and Xian.
value.literal: Emperor Wu favored them; he married an imperial clanswoman to Tuan, who served successively as prefect of Dai and Xian.

value.zh: 姚安鶴慶武定尋甸麗江元江永昌新化威遠北勝灣甸鎮康大侯瀾滄衛麓川
value.en: Yao'an, Heqing, Wuding, Xundian, Lijiang, Yuanjiang, Yongchang, Xinhua, Weiyuan, Beisheng, Wandian, Zhenkang, Dahou, Lancang Guard, and Luchuan
value.literal: Yao'an, Heqing, Wuding, Xundian, Lijiang, Yuanjiang, Yongchang, Xinhua, Weiyuan, Beisheng, Wandian, Zhenkang, Dahou, Lancang Guard, Luchuan

value.zh: 永昌，古哀牢固。
value.en: Yongchang had been the land of the ancient Ailao people.
value.literal: Yongchang was the territory of ancient Ailao.

value.zh: 漢武帝時，置不韋縣。
value.en: During the reign of Emperor Wu of Han, Buwei County was founded there.
value.literal: In the time of Emperor Wu of Han, Buwei County was established.

value.zh: 東漢置瀾滄郡，尋改永昌郡。
value.en: Under the Eastern Han a Lancang Commandery was set up, which was soon renamed Yongchang Commandery.
value.literal: In Eastern Han Lancang Commandery was established, soon renamed Yongchang Commandery.

value.zh: 唐屬姚州，後為南詔蒙氏所據，歷段氏、高氏皆為永昌府。
value.en: In Tang times it fell under Yaozhou; later the Nanzhao kingdom of the Meng clan seized it, and under the Duan and Gao dynasties in turn it was known as Yongchang Prefecture.
value.literal: In the Tang it belonged to Yaozhou; later it was seized by the Nanzhao Meng clan, and successively under the Duan and Gao clans it became Yongchang Prefecture.

value.zh: 元初，於永昌立三千戶所，隸大理萬戶府。
value.en: Early in the Yuan dynasty a Three Thousand Households Office was established at Yongchang, under the Dali Ten Thousand Households Office.
value.literal: At the beginning of the Yuan, a Three Thousand Households Office was established at Yongchang, subordinate to the Dali Ten Thousand Households Office.

value.zh: 至元間置永昌州，尋為府，隸大理路，置金齒等處宣撫司治。
value.en: In the Zhiyuan period Yongchang was first made a prefecture and soon raised to a fu, subordinate to Dali Circuit and administered by the Jinchi Pacification Commission and related offices.
value.literal: During the Zhiyuan era Yongchang Prefecture was established, soon elevated to a fu; it was subordinate to Dali Circuit, with the Jinchi Pacification Commission and other offices administering it.

value.zh: 洪武十五年定雲南，立金齒衛。
value.en: In the fifteenth year of Hongwu, after Yunnan was brought under control, the Jinchi Guard was established.
value.literal: In the fifteenth year of Hongwu Yunnan was pacified and the Jinchi Guard was established.

value.zh: 以元雲南右丞觀音保為金齒指揮使，賜姓名李觀。
value.en: The former Yuan Right Grand Councilor of Yunnan, Guanyin Bao, was appointed commander of the Jinchi Guard and given the Chinese name Li Guan.
value.literal: The Yuan Yunnan Right Grand Councilor Guanyin Bao was appointed Jinchi Commander and granted the surname and personal name Li Guan.

value.zh: 十六年，永昌州土官申保來朝，詔賜錦二匹、織金文綺二匹、衣一襲及钑花銀帶、鞾襪。
value.en: In the sixteenth year the Yongchang native official Shen Bao came to court, and the emperor bestowed on him two lengths of brocade, two lengths of gold-threaded silk, a full set of robes, an engraved silver belt, and boots and socks.
value.literal: In the sixteenth year Yongchang Prefecture native official Shen Bao came to court; an edict granted him two bolts of brocade, two bolts of gold-woven patterned silk, one set of robes, and a silver belt with chased floral patterns, plus boots and socks.

value.zh: 十七年以申保為永昌府同知。
value.en: In the seventeenth year Shen Bao was made vice prefect of Yongchang.
value.literal: In the seventeenth year Shen Bao was appointed Vice Prefect of Yongchang Prefecture.

value.zh: 四月，金齒土官段惠遣把事及其子弟來貢，賜綺帛鈔有差。
value.en: In the fourth month the Jinchi native official Duan Hui sent his steward together with sons and younger brothers to present tribute, and they received graded gifts of silk and paper money.
value.literal: In the fourth month Jinchi native official Duan Hui sent a steward and his sons and younger brothers to present tribute; gifts of silk and paper money were granted in varying amounts.

value.zh: 置施甸長官司，以土酋阿幹為副長官，賜冠帶。
value.en: The Shidian Native Office was created, the chieftain A'gan was made its deputy headman, and he was invested with official cap and belt.
value.literal: The Shidian Native Office was established, with tribal chieftain A'gan appointed deputy native official and granted cap and belt.

value.zh: 列傳第七
value.en: the seventh year of Biographies
value.literal: Biographies 7

value.zh: 孫處字季高，會稽永興人也。
value.en: Sun Chu, courtesy name Jigao, came from Yongxing in Kuaiji.
value.literal: Sun Chu, styled Jigao, was a man of Yongxing in Kuaiji.

value.zh: 籍注字，故以字行。
value.en: The household register recorded his courtesy name, so he went by it.
value.literal: Household register noted the style, so he was known by the style.

value.zh: 少任氣，武帝征孫恩，季高樂從。
value.en: Hot-blooded in youth, he eagerly joined the campaign against Sun En.
value.literal: In youth he was spirited; when Emperor Wu campaigned against Sun En, Jigao gladly followed.

value.zh: 及平建鄴，封新夷縣五等侯。
value.en: After Jiankang fell he received the fifth-rank marquisate of Xinyi.
value.literal: When Jiankang was pacified he was enfeoffed Fifth-rank Marquis of Xinyi.

value.zh: 盧循之難，武帝謂季高曰：「此賊行破，非卿不能破其窟穴。」
value.en: During Lu Xun's crisis the emperor told him, "This rebel is nearly finished—only you can destroy his lair."
value.literal: In Lu Xun's crisis the Emperor said to Jigao, "This bandit is about to break—only you can smash his nest."

value.zh: 即遣季高泛海襲番禺，拔之。
value.en: He sent Jigao by sea against Panyu and captured it.
value.literal: He at once sent Jigao by sea to strike Panyu and took it.

value.zh: 循父嘏、長史孫建之、司馬虞尪夫等輕舟奔始興，即分遣振武將軍沈田子等討平嶺表諸郡。
value.en: Xun's father Gu, chief clerk Sun Jianzhi, and marshal Yu Kuangfu fled by light boat to Shixing; Jigao sent Shen Tianzi to pacify the southern commanderies.
value.literal: Xun's father Gu, Chief Clerk Sun Jianzhi, and Marshal Yu Kuangfu and others fled in light boats to Shixing; he then sent General Who Quells the Barbarians Shen Tianzi and others to pacify the Lingnan commanderies.

value.zh: 循于左裏走還襲廣州，季高破走之。
value.en: Xun doubled back from Zuoli to hit Guangzhou; Jigao beat him off.
value.literal: Xun at Zuoli fled back to strike Guangzhou; Jigao defeated and drove him off.

value.zh: 義熙七年，季高卒，追贈南海太守，封候官縣侯。
value.en: In the seventh year of Yixi Jigao died; posthumously he was made administrator of Nanhai and marquis of Houguan.
value.literal: In the seventh year of Yixi Jigao died; posthumously he was given Administrator of Nanhai and enfeoffed Marquis of Houguan.

value.zh: 九年，武帝表贈交州刺史。
value.en: the ninth year of In the emperor posthumously made him inspector of Jiao.
value.literal: In the ninth year the Emperor memorialized giving him the post of Inspector of Jiao.

value.zh: 李安人
value.en: Li Anren
value.literal: Li Anren

value.zh: 祖嶷，衛軍將軍。
value.en: His grandfather Yi served as General of the Guards.
value.literal: His grandfather Yi was General of the Guards.

value.zh: 父欽之，薛令。
value.en: His father Qinzhi served as magistrate of Xue.
value.literal: His father Qinzhi was magistrate of Xue.

value.zh: 後為廣陵太守，行南兗州事。
value.en: He was later made Administrator of Guangling and exercised authority over South Yan Province.
value.literal: Later he became Administrator of Guangling and acted as overseer of South Yan Province affairs.

value.zh: 齊高帝在淮陰，安人遙相結事。
value.en: While Emperor Gao of Qi was still at Huaiyin, Li Anren sought him out from a distance and pledged his support.
value.literal: When the Qi Emperor Gao was at Huaiyin, Anren from afar entered into alliance with him.

value.zh: 元徽初，除司州刺史，領義陽太守。
value.en: At the opening of the Yuanhui reign he was named Inspector of Si Province and also held the post of Administrator of Yiyang.
value.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanhui era he was appointed Inspector of Si Province and concurrently Administrator of Yiyang.

value.zh: 及桂陽王休范起事，安人遣軍援都。
value.en: When Prince Xiufan of Guiyang rebelled, Li Anren dispatched forces to relieve the capital.
value.literal: When Prince Xiufan of Guiyang rose in rebellion, Anren sent troops to aid the capital.

value.zh: 建平王景素起兵，安人破其軍于葛橋。
value.en: Prince Jingsu of Jianping took up arms; Li Anren destroyed his force at Ge Bridge.
value.literal: When Prince Jingsu of Jianping raised troops, Anren routed his army at Ge Bridge.

value.zh: 景素誅，留安人行南徐州事。
value.en: Once Jingsu had been put to death, Li Anren was left in charge of South Xu Province.
value.literal: After Jingsu was executed, Anren was retained to oversee South Xu Province affairs.

value.zh: 城局參軍王回素為安人所親，盜絹二匹。
value.en: Wang Hui, a bureau staff officer whom Li Anren had long favored, stole two bolts of silk.
value.literal: Wang Hui, a staff officer of the city bureau whom Anren favored, stole two bolts of silk.

value.zh: 安人流涕謂曰：「我與卿契闊備嘗，今日犯王法，乃卿負我也。」
value.en: Li Anren wept and told him, "We have been through everything together; by breaking the law today you are the one who has betrayed our bond."
value.literal: Anren wept and said to him, "You and I have shared every hardship; today you have violated the royal law—it is you who have failed me."

value.zh: 於軍門斬之，厚為斂祭，軍府皆震服。
value.en: He had Wang Hui executed at the camp gate, then buried him with full honors. Every office in the command submitted in awe.
value.literal: He had him beheaded at the army gate, gave him a lavish funeral, and the entire headquarters trembled in submission.

value.zh: 轉東中郎司馬，行會稽郡事。
value.en: He was transferred to Eastern Staff Major and governed Kuaiji commandery in an acting capacity.
value.literal: He was transferred to Eastern Staff Major and acted as overseer of Kuaiji commandery affairs.

value.zh: 時蒼梧縱虐，齊高帝憂迫無計。
value.en: The Cangwu emperor was then raging in tyranny, and Emperor Gao of Qi, desperate and without a strategy,
value.literal: At that time the Cangwu emperor ran wild in cruelty, and Emperor Gao of Qi was pressed with worry and had no plan.

value.zh: 安人白高帝，欲于東奉江夏王躋起兵。
value.en: Li Anren urged Emperor Gao to proclaim Prince Ji of Jiangxia in the east and march against the throne.
value.literal: Anren told the Emperor Gao that he wished to raise troops in the east under Prince Ji of Jiangxia.

value.zh: 高帝不許，乃止。
value.en: Emperor Gao refused, and the plan went no further.
value.literal: The Emperor Gao did not consent, and so he stopped.

value.zh: 高帝即位，為中領軍，封康樂侯。
value.en: When Emperor Gao ascended the throne, Anren became Central General-in-Chief and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Kangle.
value.literal: When Emperor Gao ascended the throne, Anren became Central General-in-Chief and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Kangle.

value.zh: 自宋泰始以來，內外頻有賊寇，將帥以下，各募部曲，屯聚都下。
value.en: Since the Taishi era of Song, rebels and invaders had frequently appeared inside and outside the realm. Commanders and generals down the ranks each recruited retainers and gathered them in garrisons around the capital.
value.literal: Since the Taishi era of Song, there had frequently been rebels and invaders inside and outside the realm, and commanders and generals down the ranks each recruited retainers and gathered them in garrisons around the capital.

value.zh: 安人上表，以為自非淮北常備，其外餘軍悉皆輸遣，若親近宜立隨身者，聽限人數。
value.en: Anren submitted a memorial saying that except for the standing defenses north of the Huai, all other troops should be sent away. If close attendants needed personal followers, the number should be limited.
value.literal: Anren submitted a memorial saying that except for the standing defenses north of the Huai, all other remaining troops should be sent away; if close attendants needed to establish personal followers, the number should be limited.

value.zh: 上納之，故詔斷眾募。
value.en: The emperor accepted this, and an edict cut off the many recruitments.
value.literal: The emperor accepted this, and so an edict cut off the many recruitments.

value.zh: 時王敬則以勳誠見親，至於家國密事，上唯與安人論議。
value.en: At the time Wang Jingze was treated with intimacy because of his merit and sincerity, but when it came to confidential affairs of house and state, the emperor discussed them only with Anren.
value.literal: At the time Wang Jingze was treated with intimacy because of his merit and sincerity, but when it came to confidential affairs of house and state, the emperor discussed them only with Anren.

value.zh: 謂曰：「署事有卿名，我便不復細覽也。」
value.en: He told him, "If your name is on a signed matter, I no longer examine it in detail."
value.literal: He told him, "If your name is on a signed matter, I no longer examine it in detail."

value.zh: 尋為領軍將軍。
value.en: Soon he became General-in-Chief.
value.literal: Soon he became General-in-Chief.

value.zh: 魏攻壽春至馬頭，詔安人禦之，魏軍退，安人沿淮進壽春。
value.en: When Wei attacked Shouchun and reached Matou, an edict ordered Anren to resist them. The Wei army withdrew, and Anren advanced along the Huai to Shouchun.
value.literal: When Wei attacked Shouchun and reached Matou, an edict ordered Anren to resist them; the Wei army withdrew, and Anren advanced along the Huai to Shouchun.

value.zh: 先是宋時亡命王元初聚黨六合山，僭大號。
value.en: Earlier, during Song, the fugitive Wang Yuanchu had gathered followers at Liuhe Mountain and usurped a grand title.
value.literal: Earlier, during Song, the fugitive Wang Yuanchu had gathered followers at Liuhe Mountain and usurped a grand title.

value.zh: 自雲垂手過膝。
value.en: He claimed that when he lowered his hands they passed his knees.
value.literal: He claimed that when he lowered his hands they passed his knees.

value.zh: 州郡討不能禽，積十餘年。
value.en: The provinces and commanderies campaigned against him but could not capture him, and this went on for more than ten years.
value.literal: The provinces and commanderies campaigned against him but could not capture him, and this went on for more than ten years.

value.zh: 安人生禽之，斬建康市。
value.en: Anren captured him alive and beheaded him in the Jiankang marketplace.
value.literal: Anren captured him alive and beheaded him in the Jiankang marketplace.

value.zh: 高帝崩，遺詔加侍中。
value.en: When Emperor Gao died, his final edict added the office of Attendant-in-Ordinary to Anren.
value.literal: When Emperor Gao died, his final edict added the office of Attendant-in-Ordinary to Anren.

value.zh: 武帝即位，為丹陽尹，遷尚書左僕射。
value.en: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, Anren became Intendant of Danyang and was transferred to Left Director of the Masters of Writing.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, Anren became Intendant of Danyang and was transferred to Left Director of the Masters of Writing.

value.zh: 安人時屢啟密謀見賞，又善結尚書令王儉，故世傳儉啟有此授。
value.en: At the time Anren was repeatedly rewarded for submitting secret plans and was also good at forming ties with Wang Jian, Director of the Masters of Writing, so people said that Jian had recommended this appointment.
value.literal: At the time Anren was repeatedly rewarded for submitting secret plans and was also good at forming ties with Wang Jian, Director of the Masters of Writing, so people said that Jian had recommended this appointment.

value.zh: 尋上表，以年疾求退，為吳興太守。
value.en: Soon he submitted a memorial requesting retirement because of age and illness, and he became Administrator of Wuxing.
value.literal: Soon he submitted a memorial requesting retirement because of age and illness, and he became Administrator of Wuxing.

value.zh: 于家載米往郡，時服其清。
value.en: He loaded rice from his own household to take to the commandery, and people of the time admired his purity.
value.literal: He loaded rice from his own household to take to the commandery, and people of the time admired his purity.

value.zh: 吳興有項羽神護郡聽事，太守到郡，必須祀以軛下牛。
value.en: In Wuxing there was a spirit of Xiang Yu that guarded the commandery audience hall. When an administrator arrived in the commandery, he had to sacrifice a yoke-ox to it.
value.literal: In Wuxing there was a spirit of Xiang Yu that guarded the commandery audience hall; when an administrator arrived in the commandery, he had to sacrifice a yoke-ox to it.

value.zh: 安人奉佛法，不與神牛，著屐上聽事，又於聽上八關齋。
value.en: Anren followed the Buddhist law and did not give the spirit an ox. Wearing clogs, he went up into the audience hall and also held an Eight Precepts fast there.
value.literal: Anren followed the Buddhist law and did not give the spirit an ox; wearing clogs, he went up into the audience hall and also held an Eight Precepts fast there.

value.zh: 俄而牛死葬廟側，今呼為李公牛塚。
value.en: Soon afterward the ox died and was buried beside the shrine; it is now called Lord Li's Ox Mound.
value.literal: Soon afterward the ox died and was buried beside the shrine; it is now called Lord Li's Ox Mound.

value.zh: 安人尋卒，世以神為祟。
value.en: Anren died soon afterward, and people of the age thought the spirit had brought calamity on him.
value.literal: Anren died soon afterward, and people of the age thought the spirit had brought calamity on him.

value.zh: 諡肅侯。
value.en: His posthumous title was Marquis Su.
value.literal: His posthumous title was Marquis Su.

value.zh: 為人樸澀，欲就高帝求州，比及見，竟不涉一語。
value.en: Simple and awkward, he meant to beg Emperor Gao for a provincial post, yet when they met he never broached the topic.
value.literal: By nature he was plain and dull; he wished to ask Emperor Gao for a province, but when he came before him he did not manage a single word on the subject.

value.zh: 帝以其不閑政事，竟不用。
value.en: The emperor judged him unfit for civil rule and gave him nothing.
value.literal: The emperor, seeing he was unskilled in government affairs, in the end did not employ him.

value.zh: 後求竟陵郡，不知所以置辭，親人授之辭百餘言，度習誦數日，皆得上口。
value.en: He later sought Jingling commandery. Unable to frame a petition, relatives coached him in a speech of a hundred-odd lines; he drilled for days until it flowed.
value.literal: Later he sought Jingling commandery but did not know how to phrase his request; kinsmen supplied him with a speech of more than a hundred words, which Du studied for several days until he could recite it fluently.

value.zh: 會高帝履行石頭城，度於大眾中欲自陳，臨時卒忘所教，乃大言曰：「度啟公，度啟公，度無食。」
value.en: During an imperial tour of Stone City, Jiao Du tried to address the court in public, forgot every coached line, and blurted, "Du reports, my lord—Du reports—Du has no food!"
value.literal: When Emperor Gao was inspecting Stone City, Du wished to speak before the crowd but at the last moment forgot what he had been taught and cried out loudly, "Du reports to my lord, Du reports to my lord—Du has no food."

value.zh: 帝笑曰：「卿何憂無食。」
value.en: The emperor laughed. "Why fear hunger?"
value.literal: The emperor laughed and said, "Why should you worry about having no food?"

value.zh: 即賜米百斛。
value.en: He granted a hundred piculs of grain on the spot.
value.literal: He immediately granted a hundred piculs of grain.

value.zh: 建元四年，乃除淮陵太守。
value.en: Only in the fourth year of Jianyuan was he named Administrator of Huailing.
value.literal: In the fourth year of Jianyuan he was at last appointed Administrator of Huailing.

value.zh: 性好酒，醉輒暴怒，上常使人節之。
value.en: He drank heavily; in his cups he turned savage, and the throne repeatedly sent men to curb him.
value.literal: He loved wine by nature; drunk he would fly into violent rage, and the emperor often sent men to restrain him.

value.zh: 年雖老而氣力如故，除遊擊將軍，卒。
value.en: Age did not sap his strength. He was made General Who Roams in Attack, then died.
value.literal: Though old in years his strength was as before; he was appointed General Who Roams in Attack and died.

value.zh: 曹武字士威，下邳人也。
value.en: Cao Wu, styled Shiwei, was a man of Xiapi.
value.literal: Cao Wu, styled Shiwei, was a man of Xiapi.

value.zh: 本名虎頭。
value.en: His original name was Hutou.
value.literal: His original name was Hutou.

value.zh: 齊高帝鎮東府，使武與戴僧靜各領白直三百人。
value.en: When Emperor Gao of Qi garrisoned the Eastern Headquarters, he had Wu and Dai Sengjing each command three hundred white-duty guards.
value.literal: When Emperor Gao of Qi garrisoned the Eastern Headquarters, he had Wu and Dai Sengjing each command three hundred white-duty guards.

value.zh: 後為屯騎校尉，帶南城令。
value.en: Later Wu became Colonel of Garrison Cavalry and concurrently Magistrate of Nancheng.
value.literal: Later Wu became Colonel of Garrison Cavalry and concurrently Magistrate of Nancheng.

value.zh: 石頭平，封羅江縣男。
value.en: When Stone Fort was pacified, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Luojiang County.
value.literal: When Stone Fort was pacified, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Luojiang County.

value.zh: 及高帝受禪，改封監利縣。
value.en: When Emperor Gao received the abdication, Wu's fief was changed to Jianli County.
value.literal: When Emperor Gao received the abdication, Wu's fief was changed to Jianli County.

value.zh: 武帝即位，累遷驍騎將軍。
value.en: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, Wu rose through successive promotions to General of Agile Cavalry.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, Wu was repeatedly promoted, reaching General of Agile Cavalry.

value.zh: 帝以虎頭名鄙，敕改之。
value.en: The emperor considered the name Hutou vulgar and ordered him to change it.
value.literal: The emperor considered the name Hutou vulgar and ordered him to change it.

value.zh: 郁林即位，進號前將軍。
value.en: When Yulin ascended the throne, Wu's title was advanced to General of the Van.
value.literal: When Yulin ascended the throne, Wu's title was advanced to General of the Van.

value.zh: 隆昌元年，為雍州刺史。
value.en: In the first year of Longchang, he became Inspector of Yongzhou.
value.literal: In the first year of Longchang, he became Inspector of Yongzhou.

value.zh: 建武二年，進爵為侯。
value.en: In the second year of Jianwu (495), his title was advanced to marquis.
value.literal: In the second year of Jianwu, his title was advanced to marquis.

value.zh: 東昏即位，為前將軍、鎮軍司馬。
value.en: When Donghun ascended the throne, Wu became General of the Van and Sima of the Pacifying Army.
value.literal: When Donghun ascended the throne, Wu became General of the Van and Sima of the Pacifying Army.

value.zh: 永元元年，始安王遙光反，武領軍屯青溪大橋，事寧，轉散騎常侍、右衛將軍。
value.en: In the first year of Yongyuan (499), when Prince Yaoguang of Shi'an rebelled, Wu led troops to garrison the Qingxi Great Bridge. When the affair was pacified, he was transferred to Cavalier Attendant and General of the Right Guard.
value.literal: In the first year of Yongyuan, when Prince Yaoguang of Shi'an rebelled, Wu led troops to garrison the Qingxi Great Bridge; when the affair was pacified, he was transferred to Cavalier Attendant and General of the Right Guard.

value.zh: 列傳第五十三
value.en: the 53th year of Biographies
value.literal: Biographies, Number Fifty-Three

value.zh: 神念少善騎射，及老不衰。
value.en: Shennian had been skilled in horsemanship and archery since youth, and even in old age he had not lost his edge.
value.literal: Shennian from youth was skilled in mounted archery, and even when old he did not decline.

value.zh: 嘗于武帝前手執二刀楯，左右交度，馭馬往來，冠絕群伍。
value.en: Once before Emperor Wu he took two sabers and shields in hand, crossing them left and right as he drove his horse to and fro—a feat unmatched in the whole company.
value.literal: Once before Emperor Wu he held two sabers and shields in his hands, crossing them left and right, driving his horse back and forth, surpassing all the ranks.

value.zh: 時復有楊華者，能作驚軍騎，亦一時妙捷，帝深賞之。
value.en: At the same time there was Yang Hua, who could perform startling cavalry feats—another marvel of the day whom the Emperor greatly admired.
value.literal: At the same time there was also Yang Hua, who could perform startling cavalry maneuvers; he too was a marvel of agility for the age, and the Emperor deeply admired him.

value.zh: 華本名白花，武都仇池人。
value.en: Hua had originally been named Bai Hua and came from Chouchi in Wudu.
value.literal: Hua's original name was Bai Hua; he was a man of Chouchi in Wudu.

value.zh: 父大眼為魏名將。
value.en: His father Dahuan was a celebrated Wei general.
value.literal: His father Dahuan was a famous general of Wei.

value.zh: 華少有勇力，容貌瑰偉，魏胡太后逼幸之。
value.en: In youth Hua was brave and powerfully built, with a striking appearance; Empress Dowager Hu of the Northern Wei took him as her lover.
value.literal: Hua in youth had courage and strength, and his appearance was magnificent; Empress Dowager Hu of Wei forced her favor upon him.

value.zh: 華懼禍，及大眼死，擁部曲，載父屍，改名華，來降。
value.en: Fearing ruin, Hua waited until Dahuan died, then gathered his followers, bore his father's body away, changed his name to Hua, and defected to the Liang.
value.literal: Hua feared disaster; when Dahuan died he gathered his troops, loaded his father's corpse, changed his name to Hua, and came to surrender.

value.zh: 胡太后追思不已，為作楊白花歌辭，使宮人晝夜連臂蹋蹄歌之，聲甚淒斷。
value.en: Empress Dowager Hu could not stop mourning him; she had the lyrics of the Song of Yang Bai Hua written and set palace women to link arms and stamp their feet in song day and night—the melody was heartbreakingly sad.
value.literal: Empress Dowager Hu could not cease her longing and composed the lyrics of the Song of Yang Bai Hua, ordering palace women day and night to link arms and stamp their feet singing it; the sound was exceedingly mournful and broken.

value.zh: 華後位太子左衛率，卒于侯景軍中。
value.en: Hua later served as Commander of the Left Guard of the Heir Apparent and died in Hou Jing's forces.
value.literal: Hua later held the post of Commander of the Left Guard of the Heir Apparent and died in Hou Jing's army.

value.zh: 侃以大通三年至建鄴，授徐州刺史，並其兄默及三弟忱、給、元皆拜刺史。
value.en: Kan reached Jianye in the third year of Datong. He was made governor of Xuzhou, and his elder brother Mo and younger brothers Chen, Gei, and Yuan were each given a provincial governorship as well.
value.literal: Kan in the third year of Datong arrived at Jianye; he was appointed Governor of Xuzhou, and together with his elder brother Mo and his three younger brothers Chen, Gei, and Yuan all were invested as governors.

value.zh: 侃封高昌縣侯，累遷太子左衛率，中。
value.en: He was created Marquis of Gaoxiang County and rose in successive appointments to Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard.
value.literal: He was created Marquis of Gaoxiang County and rose in successive appointments to Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard.

value.zh: 車駕幸樂游苑，侃預宴。
value.en: When the emperor visited Leyou Park, Kan was among those invited to the feast.
value.literal: The imperial carriage visited Leyou Park; Kan was present at the banquet.

value.zh: 時少府奏新造兩刃矟成，長二丈四尺，圍一尺三寸。
value.en: The Chamberlain of Palace Revenues announced that a new double-edged spear had been completed: twenty-four feet long with a shaft a foot and three inches around.
value.literal: At that time the Chamberlain for the Palace Revenues reported that a newly made double-edged spear was complete — length two zhang four chi, girth one chi three cun.

value.zh: 帝因賜侃河南國紫騮令試之。
value.en: The emperor gave Kan a famed purple horse from Henan and told him to put the weapon through its paces.
value.literal: The emperor thereupon bestowed on Kan a purple stallion from Henan Commandery and ordered him to test it.

value.zh: 侃執矟上馬，左右擊刺，特盡其妙。
value.en: Kan mounted with the spear in hand and struck right and left with perfect mastery of the weapon.
value.literal: Kan took the spear, mounted, and thrust and stabbed to left and right, displaying its artistry to the utmost.

value.zh: 觀者登樹。
value.en: Spectators scrambled up into the trees for a better view.
value.literal: Those watching climbed trees.

value.zh: 帝曰：「此樹必為侍中折矣。」
value.en: The emperor remarked, "That tree won't survive the Attendant-in-Ordinary's display."
value.literal: The emperor said: "This tree will surely be broken by the Attendant-in-Ordinary."

value.zh: 俄而果折，因號此矟為折樹矟。
value.en: Sure enough, the tree soon snapped, and from then on the spear was called the Tree-Breaker.
value.literal: Before long it indeed broke, and so this spear was named the Tree-Breaking Spear.

value.zh: 北人降者，唯侃是衣冠餘緒，帝寵之踰於他者，謂曰：「朕少時捉矟，形勢似卿，今失其舊體，殊覺不奇。」
value.en: Of all the northern defectors, only Kan came from the old gentry in cap and gown. The emperor favored him above the rest and said, "When I was young my spear-play looked much like yours. These days I've lost that old form, and by comparison nothing seems quite so marvelous."
value.literal: Among northerners who had surrendered, only Kan was descended from the robe-and-cap elite; the emperor favored him beyond the others and said: "In my youth when I wielded the spear my form resembled yours; now having lost my former build, I find it quite lacking in wonder."

value.zh: 上又制武宴詩三十韻示侃，侃即席上應詔。
value.en: The emperor then composed a thirty-couplet poem for the martial banquet and presented it to Kan, who answered on the spot from his seat.
value.literal: The emperor also composed a thirty-rhyme Martial Banquet Poem and showed it to Kan; Kan immediately at the feast responded to the imperial command.

value.zh: 帝覽曰：「吾聞仁者有勇，今見勇者有仁，可謂鄒、魯遺風，英賢不絕。」
value.en: After reading it the emperor said, "They say the humane are brave; today I see bravery joined with humanity — the spirit of the sages of Zou and Lu still lives, and worthy men are not extinct."
value.literal: The emperor on reading said: "I have heard that the benevolent have courage; now I see one courageous who also has benevolence — truly the lingering wind of Zou and Lu, noble worthies never exhausted."

value.zh: 是日詔入直殿省，啟尚方仗不堪用。
