value.en: That same day he was ordered into attendance at the Palace Secretariat, where he reported that the weapons in the imperial armory were shoddy and unusable.
value.literal: That day he was ordered to enter and stand duty in the Palace Secretariat; he reported that the arsenal weapons were unfit for use.

value.zh: 上大怒，坐者非一。
value.en: The emperor flew into a rage, and several officials present were held accountable.
value.literal: The emperor was greatly angered; more than one person present was punished.

value.zh: 及侯景作逆，果弊於仗粗。
value.en: When Hou Jing rose in rebellion, the dynasty paid dearly for those worthless arms.
value.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, they indeed suffered disaster from the crude quality of the weapons.

value.zh: 二年，復為都官尚書。
value.en: The following year he was again appointed Minister of Justice.
value.literal: In the second year he again became Minister of the Ministry of Justice.

value.zh: 侯景反，攻陷曆陽，帝問侃討景之策。
value.en: When Hou Jing rebelled and took Liyang, the emperor asked Kan how best to destroy him.
value.literal: Hou Jing rebelled, captured Liyang, and the emperor asked Kan for a strategy to suppress Jing.

value.zh: 侃求以二千人急據採石，令邵陵王襲取壽春，使景進不得前，退失巢窟，烏合之眾，自然瓦解。
value.en: Kan asked for two thousand men to seize Caishi immediately and urged the Prince of Shaoling to take Shouchun by surprise, so Hou Jing could neither advance nor retreat to a secure base; his ragtag following would fall apart on its own.
value.literal: Kan requested two thousand men to seize Caishi in haste, and ordered the Prince of Shaoling to strike and take Shouchun, so that Jing advancing could not proceed and retreating would lose his nest — the mob gathered at random would naturally disintegrate.

value.zh: 議者謂景未敢便逼都，遂寢其策。
value.en: The counsellors argued that Hou Jing would never dare march straight on the capital, and Kan's plan was set aside.
value.literal: Those in council said Jing would not dare promptly press on the capital, and so his plan was shelved.

value.zh: 令王質往。
value.en: They sent Wang Zhi in his place.
value.literal: Wang Zhi was ordered to go instead.

value.zh: 侃曰：「今茲敗矣。」
value.en: Kan said, "We've lost already."
value.literal: Kan said: "This time we are defeated."

value.zh: 乃令侃率千餘騎頓望國門。
value.en: Kan was then ordered to take a thousand-plus cavalry and hold position before the Capital Gate.
value.literal: He was then ordered to lead more than a thousand horsemen and encamp facing the Capital Gate.

value.zh: 景至新林，追侃入副宣城王都督城內諸軍事。
value.en: When Hou Jing reached Xinlin, Kan was rushed inside to serve as deputy to the Prince of Xuancheng in commanding the city's defenses.
value.literal: When Jing reached Xinlin, Kan was urgently summoned to enter the city as deputy to the Prince of Xuancheng in directing all military affairs within the walls.

value.zh: 賊既頻攻不捷，乃築長圍。
value.en: After repeated assaults failed, the rebels settled in to build a full circumvallation.
value.literal: Since the rebels had repeatedly attacked without success, they then built a long encirclement.

value.zh: 朱異、張綰議出擊之。
value.en: Zhu Yi and Zhang Wan urged a sortie against the encirclement.
value.literal: Zhu Yi and Zhang Wan debated sallying out to strike them.

value.zh: 帝以問侃，侃曰：「不可，賊多日攻城，既不能下，故立長圍，欲引城中降者耳。
value.en: The emperor asked Kan's view. Kan said, "No. They have failed to take the city by assault, so they are building a long siege line to tempt defectors inside the walls — that is all.
value.literal: The emperor questioned Kan; Kan said: "It cannot be done. The rebels have besieged for many days and could not take the city, so they establish a long encirclement intending only to lure those in the city who would surrender.

value.zh: 今擊之，出人若少，不足破賊；
value.en: If we sortie with too few men, we won't break them;
value.literal: If we strike now and send out few men, it is insufficient to break the rebels;

value.zh: 若多，則一旦失利，門隘橋小，必大致挫衄。」
value.en: but if we send out many and lose, the gates are narrow and the bridges small — a retreat would become a slaughter."
value.literal: if many, then once defeated the gates are narrow and the bridges small — there will surely be great rout and disaster."

value.zh: 不從，遂使千餘人出戰。
value.en: His counsel was ignored, and more than a thousand men were sent out to fight.
value.literal: The advice was not followed; more than a thousand men were then sent out to battle.

value.zh: 未及交鋒，望風退走，果以爭橋赴水，死者太半。
value.en: They never even closed with the enemy but broke and ran. In the crush at the bridge men tumbled into the water, and more than half perished.
value.literal: Before they could cross blades they fled at sight of the enemy; indeed in the scramble for the bridge they plunged into the water — more than half died.

value.zh: 羊鴉仁字孝穆，泰山钜平人也。
value.en: Yang Ren, courtesy name Xiaomu, was a native of Juping in Taishan commandery.
value.literal: Yang Ren, styled Xiaomu, was a man of Juping in Taishan.

value.zh: 少驍勇，仕郡為主簿。
value.en: As a young man he was bold and brave and served his commandery as chief clerk.
value.literal: In youth he was valiant and brave; in the commandery he served as Chief Clerk.

value.zh: 並通中，率兄弟自魏歸梁，封廣晉侯。
value.en: In the Datong era he led his brothers in defecting from Wei to the Liang and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Guangjin.
value.literal: In the Datong era he led his brothers in coming from Wei to Liang and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Guangjin.

value.zh: 征伐青、齊間，累有功績，位至都督、北司州刺史。
value.en: On campaigns between Qing and Qi he won repeated distinction, rising to area commander and Inspector of Northern Sizhou.
value.literal: Campaigning between Qing and Qi he repeatedly achieved merit, rising to Grand Commander and Inspector of Northern Sizhou.

value.zh: 及侯景降，詔鴉仁督土州刺史桓和之、仁州刺史湛海珍等趣縣瓠應接。
value.en: When Hou Jing submitted, Ren was ordered to lead Inspector of Tuzhou Huan Hezhi, Inspector of Renzhou Zhan Haizhen, and others to Xuanhuo to coordinate support.
value.literal: When Hou Jing surrendered, an edict ordered Ren to direct Inspector of Tuzhou Huan Hezhi, Inspector of Renzhou Zhan Haizhen, and others to hasten to Xuanhuo to link up in support.

value.zh: 景至，仍為都督、司豫二州刺史，鎮縣瓠。
value.en: When Hou Jing arrived, Ren remained area commander and Inspector of Si and Yu provinces, holding Xuanhuo.
value.literal: When Jing arrived, he remained Grand Commander and Inspector of the two provinces Si and Yu, garrisoning Xuanhuo.

value.zh: 會侯景敗于渦陽，魏軍漸逼，鴉仁恐糧運不繼，遂還北司，上表陳謝。
value.en: When Hou Jing was defeated at Woyang and Wei forces closed in, Ren, fearing his supply lines would fail, withdrew to Northern Sizhou and submitted a confession to the throne.
value.literal: It happened that Hou Jing was defeated at Woyang; Wei armies gradually pressed in; Ren feared grain supply would not continue, so he returned to Northern Sizhou and submitted a memorial confessing fault.

value.zh: 帝大怒鴉仁，鴉仁懼，頓軍於淮上。
value.en: The emperor was furious with Ren. Afraid, he halted his army on the Huai.
value.literal: The emperor was greatly angry at Ren; Ren was afraid and halted his army on the Huai.

value.zh: 及侯景反，鴉仁率所部入援。
value.en: When Hou Jing rose in rebellion, Ren led his troops to the capital's relief.
value.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, Ren led his division to enter as relief.

value.zh: 戴法興 徐爰 阮佃夫 紀僧真 劉系宗 茹法亮 呂文顯 茹法珍 周石珍 陸驗 司馬申 施文慶 沈客卿 孔範
value.en: Dai Faxing, Xu Ai, Ruan Dianfu, Ji Sengzhen, Liu Xizong, Ru Faliang, Lü Wenxian, Ru Fazhen, Zhou Shizhen, Lu Yan, Sima Shen, Shi Wenqing, Shen Keqing, and Kong Fan
value.literal: Dai Faxing, Xu Ai, Ruan Dianfu, Ji Sengzhen, Liu Xizong, Ru Faliang, Lü Wenxian, Ru Fazhen, Zhou Shizhen, Lu Yan, Sima Shen, Shi Wenqing, Shen Keqing, and Kong Fan

value.zh: 徐爰，字長玉，南琅邪開陽人也。
value.en: Xu Ai, styled Changyu, came from Kaiyang in Southern Langye.
value.literal: Xu Ai, style name Changyu, was a native of Kaiyang in Southern Langye.

value.zh: 本名瑗，後以與傅亮父同名，亮啟改為爰。
value.en: He was originally named Yuan; because this matched the name of Fu Liang's father, Liang petitioned to have it changed to Ai.
value.literal: His original name was Yuan; later, because it was the same as Fu Liang's father's name, Liang memorialized to have it changed to Ai.

value.zh: 初為晉琅邪王大司馬府中典軍，從北征，微密有意理，為武帝所知。
value.en: He first served as barracks officer on Prince Langye of Jin's staff; on the northern campaign his shrewd judgment won Emperor Wu's notice.
value.literal: He first served as barracks officer in the great marshal's staff of Prince Langye of Jin; on the northern campaign he showed subtle understanding and sound judgment and came to Emperor Wu's notice.

value.zh: 少帝在東宮，入侍左右。
value.en: When Emperor Shao was crown prince, Ai entered service at his side.
value.literal: When Emperor Shao was in the Eastern Palace he entered to attend at the ruler's side.

value.zh: 文帝初，又見親任，遂至殿中侍御史。
value.en: Early in Emperor Wen's reign he again won personal favor and rose to palace investigating censor.
value.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Wen's reign he was again treated with personal trust and rose to palace attendant investigating censor.

value.zh: 元嘉十二年，轉南台御史，始興王浚後軍行參軍。
value.en: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia he became a southern bureau censor and acting staff officer on Prince Shixing Jun's rear army.
value.literal: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia he was transferred to censor of the southern bureau and became acting staff officer on the rear army of Prince Shixing Jun.

value.zh: 復侍太子于東宮，遷員外散騎侍郎。
value.en: He again served the crown prince in the Eastern Palace and was promoted to supernumerary attendant cavalier.
value.literal: He again attended the crown prince in the Eastern Palace and was promoted to supernumerary attendant cavalier.

value.zh: 文帝每出軍，常懸授兵略。
value.en: Whenever Emperor Wen campaigned, he often gave Ai his battle plans in advance.
value.literal: Whenever Emperor Wen took the field he would often entrust Ai with military plans in advance.

value.zh: 二十九年，重遣王玄謨等北侵，配爰五百人，隨軍碻磝，銜中旨臨時宣示。
value.en: the twenty-ninth year of In he again sent Wang Xuanmo north; Ai was given five hundred men to accompany the army to Quepo and proclaim the emperor's secret orders as events unfolded.
value.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he again sent Wang Xuanmo and others north on campaign, assigning Ai five hundred men to follow the army to Quepo, bearing the emperor's secret intent to proclaim on the spot.

value.zh: 孝武至新亭，江夏王義恭南奔，爰時在殿內，詐劭追義恭，因即得南走。
value.en: When Emperor Xiaowu reached Xinting and Prince Jiangxia Yigong fled south, Ai was in the hall; pretending Shao was pursuing Yigong, he slipped away south as well.
value.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu reached Xinting, Prince Jiangxia Yigong fled south; Ai was then inside the hall and pretended that Shao was pursuing Yigong, thus managing to flee south himself.

value.zh: 時孝武將即大位，軍府造次，不曉朝章，爰素諳其事，及至，莫不喜悅，以兼太常丞撰立儀注。
value.en: As Emperor Xiaowu prepared to ascend the throne, the military headquarters was in chaos and knew nothing of court ritual—Ai, who knew these matters thoroughly, was welcomed with relief and made vice-director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to draft the accession ceremonies.
value.literal: At that time Emperor Xiaowu was about to take the great throne; the army headquarters was in disarray and did not understand court regulations—Ai had long been versed in such matters, and when he arrived everyone was delighted; he was made concurrently vice-director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to draft the ritual protocols for accession.

value.zh: 後兼尚書右丞，遷左丞。
value.en: He later served concurrently as right vice-director of the Secretariat and was promoted to left vice-director.
value.literal: Later he was concurrently right vice-director of the Secretariat and was promoted to left vice-director.

value.zh: 先是，元嘉中使著作郎何承天草創國史，孝武初又使奉朝請山謙之、南台御史蘇寶生踵成之。
value.en: Before this, during Yuanjia, the court had ordered Composition Gentleman He Chengtian to make a first draft of the state history; at the beginning of Xiaowu's reign it further ordered Court Gentleman Shan Qianzhi and Southern Office censor Su Baosheng to continue and complete it.
value.literal: Before this, during Yuanjia, the court had ordered Composition Gentleman He Chengtian to make a first draft of the state history; at the beginning of Xiaowu's reign it further ordered Court Gentleman Shan Qianzhi and Southern Office censor Su Baosheng to continue and complete it.

value.zh: 孝建六年，又以爰領著作郎，使終其業。
value.en: In the sixth year of Xiaojian, it again made Xu Ai acting Composition Gentleman and ordered him to finish the work.
value.literal: In the sixth year of Xiaojian, it again made Xu Ai acting Composition Gentleman and ordered him to finish the work.

value.zh: 爰雖因前作，而專為一家之書。
value.en: Although Xu Ai built on the earlier drafts, he made the book entirely his own family's work.
value.literal: Although Xu Ai built on the earlier drafts, he made the book entirely his own family's work.

value.zh: 上表「起元義熙，為王業之始，載序宣力，為功臣之斷」。
value.en: He submitted a memorial: "Begin with the first year of Yixi, taking it as the start of the royal enterprise; record and arrange those who exerted themselves, taking this as the cutoff for meritorious ministers."
value.literal: He submitted a memorial: "Begin with the first year of Yixi, taking it as the start of the royal enterprise; record and arrange those who exerted themselves, taking this as the cutoff for meritorious ministers."

value.zh: 於是內外博議。
value.en: Thereupon those inside and outside the court debated the matter broadly.
value.literal: Thereupon those inside and outside the court debated the matter broadly.

value.zh: 太宰江夏王義恭等三十五人同爰，宜以義熙元年為斷。
value.en: Grand Steward Prince Yigong of Jiangxia and thirty-four others agreed with Xu Ai that the cutoff should be the first year of Yixi.
value.literal: Grand Steward Prince Yigong of Jiangxia and thirty-four others agreed with Xu Ai that the cutoff should be the first year of Yixi.

value.zh: 散騎常侍巴陵王休若、尚書金部郎檀道鸞二人謂宜以元興三年為始。
value.en: Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary Prince Xiuruo of Baling and Tan Daoluan, Gentleman of the Treasury Section of the Secretariat, held that it should begin with the third year of Yuanxing.
value.literal: Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary Prince Xiuruo of Baling and Tan Daoluan, Gentleman of the Treasury Section of the Secretariat, held that it should begin with the third year of Yuanxing.

value.zh: 太學博士虞和謂宜以開國為宋西元年。
value.en: Imperial Academy erudite Yu He said it should take the founding of the state as the first year of Song.
value.literal: Imperial Academy erudite Yu He said it should take the founding of the state as the first year of Song.

value.zh: 詔曰：「項籍、聖公，編錄二漢，前史已有成例。桓玄傳宜在宋典，餘如爰議。」
value.en: The edict said, "Xiang Ji and Shenggong are compiled and recorded in the histories of the two Han; earlier histories already provide a settled precedent. Huan Xuan's biography should be placed in the Song records. For the rest, follow Xu Ai's proposal."
value.literal: The edict said, "Xiang Ji and Shenggong are compiled and recorded in the histories of the two Han; earlier histories already provide a settled precedent. Huan Xuan's biography should be placed in the Song records. For the rest, follow Xu Ai's proposal."

value.zh: 高帝疾甚，令僧真典遺詔。
value.en: When Emperor Gao's illness grew grave, he had Sengzhen oversee the drafting of his final testament.
value.literal: When Emperor Gao's illness grew severe, he had Sengzhen supervise the drafting of his final testament.

value.zh: 永明元年，丁父喪。
value.en: In the first year of Yongming he went into mourning for his father's death.
value.literal: In the first year of Yongming he observed mourning for his father's death.

value.zh: 起為建威將軍，尋除南泰山太守，又為舍人。
value.en: Recalled from mourning as General Who Establishes Might, he was soon appointed administrator of South Taishan and then again served as Confidential Adjunct.
value.literal: Recalled to service as General Who Establishes Might, he was soon made Administrator of South Taishan, then again served as Confidential Adjunct.

value.zh: 僧真容貌言吐，雅有士風，武帝嘗目送之，笑曰：「人生何必計門戶，紀僧真堂堂，貴人所不及也。」
value.en: Sengzhen's appearance and speech had an elegant scholar's bearing. Emperor Wu once watched him go and laughed, "In life why must one count one's lineage? Ji Sengzhen is truly imposing—noblemen cannot match him."
value.literal: Sengzhen's bearing and speech had an elegant scholar's style. Emperor Wu once watched him depart and laughed, "In life why must one count one's lineage? Ji Sengzhen is truly imposing—noblemen cannot match him."

value.zh: 諸權要中最被眄遇。
value.en: Among all the powerful favorites, he was the most favored.
value.literal: Among all the powerful favorites he was most favored with attention.

value.zh: 後除前軍將軍。
value.en: Later he was appointed General of the Vanguard.
value.literal: Later he was appointed General of the Vanguard.

value.zh: 遭母喪，開塚得五色兩頭蛇。
value.en: When his mother died, a five-colored two-headed serpent was found upon opening the tomb.
value.literal: When his mother died, upon opening the tomb a five-colored two-headed serpent was found.

value.zh: 明帝以僧真歷朝驅使，建武初，除遊擊將軍，兼司農，待之如舊。
value.en: Because Sengzhen had been employed through successive reigns, Emperor Ming, at the beginning of Jianwu, appointed him General of Mobile Cavalry and concurrently Minister of Agriculture, treating him as before.
value.literal: Because Sengzhen had been employed through successive reigns, Emperor Ming, at the beginning of Jianwu, appointed him General of Mobile Cavalry and concurrently Minister of Agriculture, treating him as before.

value.zh: 欲令僧真臨郡，僧真啟進其弟僧猛為鎮蠻護軍、晉熙太守。
value.en: The emperor wished to have Sengzhen govern a commandery, but Sengzhen memorialized recommending his younger brother Sengmeng as Protector Who Suppresses the Man and administrator of Jinxi.
value.literal: The emperor wished to have Sengzhen govern a commandery, but Sengzhen memorialized recommending his younger brother Sengmeng as Protector Who Suppresses the Man and administrator of Jinxi.

value.zh: 永泰元年，除司農卿。
value.en: In the first year of Yongtai, Sengzhen was appointed Chamberlain for the National Treasury.
value.literal: In the first year of Yongtai, Sengzhen was appointed Chamberlain for the National Treasury.

value.zh: 明帝崩，掌山陵事，出為廬陵內史。
value.en: When Emperor Ming died, he managed the mountain mausoleum affairs and was then sent out as internal administrator of Luling.
value.literal: When Emperor Ming died, he managed the mountain mausoleum affairs and was then sent out as internal administrator of Luling.

value.zh: 卒於官。
value.en: He died in office.
value.literal: He died in office.

value.zh: 僧猛後卒于晉熙太守。
value.en: Sengmeng later died while serving as administrator of Jinxi.
value.literal: Sengmeng later died while serving as administrator of Jinxi.

value.zh: 兄弟皆有風姿舉止，並善隸書。
value.en: The brothers both had graceful bearing and deportment, and both were skilled in clerical script.
value.literal: The brothers both had graceful bearing and deportment, and both were skilled in clerical script.

value.zh: 僧猛又能飛白書，作飛白賦。
value.en: Sengmeng was also skilled in flying-white script and composed a "Rhapsody on Flying-White Script."
value.literal: Sengmeng was also skilled in flying-white script and composed a "Rhapsody on Flying-White Script."

value.zh: 僧真子交卿，甚有解用。
value.en: Sengzhen's son Jiaoqing was very capable in practical matters.
value.literal: Sengzhen's son Jiaoqing was very capable in practical matters.

value.zh: 武帝崩，僧真號泣思慕。
value.en: When Emperor Wu died, Sengzhen wailed and mourned him with deep devotion.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu died, Sengzhen wailed and mourned in deep longing.

value.zh: 志第三 曆下
value.en: Treatise 3: Calendar, Part 2.
value.literal: Treatise 3, Calendar (Part 2).

value.zh: 法興議曰：「戰國橫騖，史官喪紀，爰及漢初，格候莫審，後雜覘知在南斗二十二度，元和所用，即與古曆相符也。
value.en: Dai Faxing submitted: "In the Warring States calendrical practice ran wild, historiographers lost proper reckoning; down to early Han, gnomon observations were uncertain; later mixed observation placed it at Southern Dipper 22°; the Yuanhe calendar used this, matching the ancient calendar.
value.literal: Faxing submitted: "In the Warring States era calendrical practice ran wild, historiographers lost proper reckoning; down to early Han, gnomon observations were uncertain; later mixed observation placed it at twenty-two degrees of Southern Dipper; the Yuanhe calendar used this, matching the ancient calendar.

value.zh: 逮至景初，終無毫忒。」
value.en: Down to the Jingchu era there was never the slightest error."
value.literal: Down to the Jingchu era there was never the slightest error."

value.zh: 沖之曰：古術訛雜，其詳闕聞，乙卯之曆，秦代所用，必有效於當時，故其言可征也。
value.en: Zu Chongzhi said: Ancient methods were wrong and mixed; details are missing from record; the yimao calendar was used in the Qin era and must have been effective in its time, so its words can be verified.
value.literal: Chongzhi said: Ancient methods were wrong and mixed; details are missing from record; the yimao calendar was used in the Qin era and must have been effective in its time, so its words can be verified.

value.zh: 漢武改創，檢課詳備，正儀審漏，事在前史，測星辨度，理無乖遠。
value.en: Emperor Wu of Han reformed and created anew; testing and checking were detailed and complete, correcting instruments and examining clepsydra—the matter is in earlier histories; measuring stars and distinguishing degrees, the principle is not far wrong.
value.literal: Emperor Wu of Han reformed and created anew; testing and checking were detailed and complete, correcting instruments and examining clepsydra—the matter is in earlier histories; measuring stars and distinguishing degrees, the principle is not far wrong.

value.zh: 今議者所是不實見，所非徒為虛妄，辨彼駭此，既非通談，運今背古，所誣誠多，偏據一說，未若兼今之為長也。
value.en: What the debaters approve is not real observation; what they reject is merely empty falsity; distinguishing that and rejecting this is not general discussion; applying the present while turning against antiquity, the distortions are indeed many—relying on one theory alone is not as good as combining the present.
value.literal: What the debaters approve is not real observation; what they reject is merely empty falsity; distinguishing that and rejecting this is not general discussion; applying the present and turning against antiquity, the distortions are indeed many—relying on one theory alone is not as good as combining the present.

value.zh: 《景初》之法，實錯五緯，今則在沖口，至曩已移日。
value.en: The Jingchu method in fact mis-set the five planets; Dai Faxing now cites it, yet long ago its solar day had already shifted.
value.literal: The Jingchu method in fact mis-set the five planets; now it is in Chongzhi's mouth, yet long ago the day had already shifted.

value.zh: 蓋略治朔望，無事檢候，是以晷漏昏明，並即《元和》，二分異景，尚不知革，日度微差，宜其謬矣。
value.en: It roughly handled new and full moons without testing observation; therefore gnomon, clepsydra, dusk and dawn all followed Yuanhe; at the two seasonal nodes the shadows differed, yet they still did not know to reform—a slight solar discrepancy was bound to go wrong.
value.literal: It roughly handled new and full moons without testing observation; therefore gnomon, clepsydra, dusk and dawn all followed Yuanhe; at the two seasonal nodes the shadows differed, yet they still did not know to reform—solar degree's slight discrepancy ought to have been wrong.

value.zh: 高允，字伯恭，勃海人也。
value.en: Gao Yun, whose courtesy name was Bogong, came from Bohai.
value.literal: Gao Yun, styled Bogong, was a man of Bohai.

value.zh: 祖泰，在叔父湖傳。
value.en: His grandfather Tai is discussed in the biography of his uncle Hu.
value.literal: His grandfather Tai is treated in the biography of his uncle Hu.

value.zh: 父韜，少以英朗知名，同郡封懿雅相敬慕。
value.en: His father Tao won early fame for his keen intelligence and open manner; he and Feng Yi of the same commandery held each other in deep mutual esteem.
value.literal: His father Tao was in youth renowned for brilliance and clarity; Feng Yi of the same commandery admired and respected each other in refined friendship.

value.zh: 為慕容垂太尉從事中郎。
value.en: He served Murong Chui as an attendant gentleman in the office of the grand commandant.
value.literal: He served as Attendant Gentleman in the office of the Grand Commandant under Murong Chui.

value.zh: 太祖平中山，以韜為丞相參軍。
value.en: After Emperor Daowu conquered Zhongshan, Tao was appointed an army adviser on the chancellor's staff.
value.literal: When the Taizu Emperor pacified Zhongshan, Tao was made Army Advisor to the Chancellor.

value.zh: 早卒。
value.en: He died at an early age.
value.literal: He died young.

value.zh: 夫百王之御士也，莫不資伏羣才，以隆治道。
value.en: In governing scholars, none of the hundred kings failed to rely on the host of talents to elevate the governing Way.
value.literal: Of the hundred kings' governing of scholars, none did not rely on and submit to the host of talents to elevate the governing Way.

value.zh: 故周文以多士克寧，漢武以得賢為盛。
value.en: Hence King Wen of Zhou with many scholars achieved tranquility, and Emperor Wu of Han took obtaining the worthy as his glory.
value.literal: Hence King Wen of Zhou with many scholars achieved tranquility; Emperor Wu of Han took obtaining the worthy as flourishing.

value.zh: 此載籍之所記，由來之常義。
value.en: Such is what the records memorialize—the constant meaning handed down from antiquity.
value.literal: This the records memorialize—the constant meaning from antiquity.

value.zh: 魏自神䴥已後，宇內平定，誅赫連積世之僭，掃窮髮不羇之寇，南摧江楚，西盪涼域，殊方之外，慕義而至。
value.en: From Shenqi onward Wei pacified the realm, destroyed the Herunian usurpers across generations, and swept away unrestrained barbarians; south they crushed Jiang and Chu, west they shook the Liang domains—and beyond strange regions, those who admired righteousness came.
value.literal: Wei from after Shenqi onward, within the realm was pacified; they executed the Herunian line's usurpation across generations and swept away the unrestrained barbarians of poor hair; south they crushed Jiang and Chu, west they shook the Liang domains—beyond strange regions, those who admired righteousness came.

value.zh: 於是偃兵息甲，修立文學，登延儁造，酬諮政事。
value.en: Thereupon they stilled weapons and rested armor, established literary learning, promoted outstanding men, and consulted them on government affairs.
value.literal: Thereupon they stilled weapons and rested armor, established and raised literary learning, ascended and extended outstanding makers, and rewarded and consulted on government affairs.

value.zh: 夢想賢哲，思遇其人，訪諸有司，以求名士。
value.en: They dreamed of the worthy and wise and sought to encounter such persons, inquiring of the relevant offices to seek famous scholars.
value.literal: Dreaming of the worthy and wise, they thought to encounter such persons; they inquired of the relevant offices to seek famous scholars.

value.zh: 咸稱范陽盧玄等四十二人，皆冠冕之冑，著問州邦，有羽儀之用。
value.en: All praised Lu Xuan of Fanyang and forty-two others—all scions of eminent houses, renowned in their commanderies and states, fit to serve as exemplars.
value.literal: All praised Lu Xuan of Fanyang and forty-two others—all caps and coronets' scions, renowned in their commanderies and states, with the usefulness of feathered banners.

value.zh: 親發明詔，以徵玄等。
value.en: He personally issued bright edicts summoning Xuan and the others.
value.literal: The sovereign personally issued bright edicts to summon Xuan and the others.

value.zh: 乃曠官以待之，懸爵以縻之。
value.en: They left offices vacant to await them and suspended ranks to retain them.
value.literal: They left offices vacant to await them and suspended ranks to tether them.

value.zh: 其就命三十五人，自餘依例州郡所遣者不可稱記。
value.en: Thirty-five accepted the command; the rest sent according to precedent by commanderies and states cannot be fully recorded.
value.literal: Those who accepted the command were thirty-five men; the rest sent according to precedent by commanderies and states cannot be fully recorded.

value.zh: 爾乃髦士盈朝，而濟濟之美興焉。
value.en: Then eminent scholars filled the court, and the splendor of abundance flourished.
value.literal: Then eminent scholars filled the court, and the beauty of abundance arose.

value.zh: 昔與之俱蒙斯舉，或從容廊廟，或游集私門，上談公務，下盡忻娛，以為千載一時，始於此矣。
value.en: Those who together received this summons—some at ease in court, some gathering in private homes—above discussed public affairs, below fully shared delight, thinking it a moment once in a thousand years, beginning from this.
value.literal: Formerly those who together received this summons—some at ease in the hall and temple, some gathering in private gates—above discussed public affairs, below fully shared delight, thinking it a thousand-year moment, beginning from this.

value.zh: 日月推移，吉凶代謝，同徵之人，凋殲殆盡。
value.en: Sun and moon shifted; fortune and misfortune succeeded one another; those summoned together were nearly all gone.
value.literal: Sun and moon shifted; fortune and misfortune succeeded one another; those summoned together were nearly all destroyed.

value.zh: 在者數子，然復分張。
value.en: Of those who remain, only a few—and they too are scattered apart.
value.literal: Of those who remain, a few men—yet again scattered apart.

value.zh: 往昔之忻，變為悲戚。
value.en: Former delight has changed into present sorrow.
value.literal: Former delight changed into present sorrow.

value.zh: 張仲業東臨營州，遲其還返，一敍于懷，齊衿于垂歿之年，寫情於桑榆之末。
value.en: Zhang Zhongye governed Yingzhou in the east; I longed for his return and once poured out my heart to him; together we grieved as death approached, writing our feelings at life's sunset.
value.literal: Zhang Zhongye eastward governed Yingzhou; I delayed his return and once poured out my breast; together we grieved in the year of approaching death, writing feeling at mulberry and sunset's end.

value.zh: 其人不幸，復至殞歿。
value.en: That man was unfortunate and again met death.
value.literal: That man was unfortunate and again came to perishing death.

value.zh: 在朝者皆後進之士，居里者非疇昔之人，進涉無寄心之所，出入無解顏之地。
value.en: Those in court are all later-entering scholars; those in the neighborhood are not men of former days; in advancing there is no place for the mind to rest, in going out and entering no face to unburden.
value.literal: Those in court are all later-entering scholars; those in the neighborhood are not men of former days; advancing and wading has no place for the mind to rest; going out and entering has no place to unknit the countenance.

value.zh: 顧省形骸，所以永歎而不已。
value.en: Looking back at my bodily form, I therefore sigh unceasingly.
value.literal: Looking back at my bodily form, therefore I sigh unceasingly.

value.zh: 夫頌者美盛德之形容，亦可以長言寄意。
value.en: The eulogy portrays flourishing virtue's form; one may also use extended words to lodge one's intent.
value.literal: The eulogy is the portrayal of flourishing virtue's form and appearance; one may also use long words to lodge intent.

value.zh: 不為文二十年矣，然事切於心，豈可默乎？
value.en: I have not written for twenty years, yet affairs cut to the heart—how can I remain silent?
value.literal: I have not composed writing for twenty years, yet affairs cut to the heart—how can I be silent?

value.zh: 遂為之頌，詞曰：
value.en: Thereupon I composed this eulogy; the words say:
value.literal: Thereupon I made this eulogy for them; the words say:

value.zh: 韋孝寬 韋敻 梁士彥
value.en: Biographies of Wei Xiaokuan, Wei Xiong, and Liang Shiyan
value.literal: Wei Xiaokuan; Wei Xiong; Liang Shiyan

value.zh: 建德之後，武帝志在平齊。
value.en: After the Jiande era Emperor Wu turned his mind to conquering Qi.
value.literal: After the Jiande era, Emperor Wu set his mind on pacifying Qi.

value.zh: 孝寬乃上疏陳三策。
value.en: Xiaokuan submitted a memorial presenting three strategies.
value.literal: Xiaokuan then submitted a memorial setting forth three strategies.

value.zh: 其第一策曰：
value.en: The first strategy read:
value.literal: The first strategy said:

value.zh: 書奏，武帝遣小司寇淮南西元
value.en: When the memorial was in, Emperor Wu sent Junior Minister of Crime Yuan
value.literal: The memorial was submitted; Emperor Wu sent Junior Minister of Crime Huainan Xi Yuan

value.en: [Textual note: Wei]
value.literal: (Wei) [emended variant]

value.zh: 偉、開府伊婁謙等重幣聘齊。
value.en: Wei, Kaifu Yilou Qian, and others with rich gifts to court Qi.
value.literal: 〔Wei〕 emended: Xi Yuan → Yuan Wei, Kaifu Yilou Qian, and others with heavy gifts to visit Qi as envoys.

value.zh: 爾後遂大舉，再駕而定山東，卒如孝寬之策。
value.en: Later the court did launch a great campaign. The emperor marched twice and pacified the east of the mountains, just as Xiaokuan had foreseen.
value.literal: After that a great campaign was launched; twice the emperor took the field and settled the lands east of the mountains; in the end it happened as Xiaokuan's strategy [had said].

value.zh: 孝寬每以年迫懸車，屢請致仕。
value.en: Xiaokuan, feeling his years advance, repeatedly asked to retire.
value.literal: Xiaokuan repeatedly, because his years pressed toward hanging up his chariot, asked many times to retire from office.

value.zh: 帝以海內未平，優詔弗許。
value.en: The emperor, holding that the realm was not yet fully at peace, graciously refused each request.
value.literal: The emperor, because within the seas was not yet pacified, with a gracious edict did not permit it.

value.zh: 至是復稱疾乞骸骨。
value.en: At this point he again pleaded illness and asked to be allowed to retire.
value.literal: At this point he again claimed illness and requested to retire.

value.zh: 帝曰：「往已面申本懷，何煩重請也。」
value.en: The emperor said, "You already told me your mind face to face — why ask again?"
value.literal: The emperor said: "You have already stated your intent to me in person — why trouble yourself with repeated requests?"

value.zh: 五年，帝東伐，過幸玉壁。
value.en: In the fifth year Emperor Wu marched east and, passing through, visited Yubi.
value.literal: In the fifth year the emperor marched east; passing through, he visited Yubi.

value.zh: 觀禦敵之所，深嘆羨之，移時乃去。
value.en: He inspected the enemy's old defenses, sighed in deep admiration, and lingered a long while before leaving.
value.literal: He viewed the places where the enemy had been held at bay, sighed deeply in admiration, and only after a long while departed.

value.zh: 孝寬自以習練齊人虛實，請為先驅。
value.en: Xiaokuan, who knew the Qi armies well, asked to lead the van.
value.literal: Xiaokuan, judging himself practiced in the strengths and weaknesses of the men of Qi, asked to serve as vanguard.

value.zh: 帝以玉壁要衝，非孝寬無以鎮之，乃不許。
value.en: The emperor held that Yubi was too vital to leave to anyone but Xiaokuan and refused.
value.literal: The emperor, because Yubi was a vital choke point and none but Xiaokuan could hold it, would not allow it.

value.zh: 及趙王招率兵出稽胡，與大軍掎角，乃敕孝寬為行軍總管，圍守華谷以應接之。
value.en: When Prince of Zhao Yuwen Zhao marched against the Ji Hu in pincer with the main force, Xiaokuan was ordered to act as campaign commander, besiege Huagu, and keep the link open.
value.literal: When Prince of Zhao Zhao led troops out against the Ji Hu in pincer coordination with the main army, he thereupon ordered Xiaokuan to be campaign commander, to besiege and hold Huagu in support.

value.zh: 孝寬克其四城。
value.en: Xiaokuan took four of their cities.
value.literal: Xiaokuan captured four of their cities.

value.zh: 武帝平晉州，復令孝寬還舊鎮。
value.en: After Emperor Wu took Jin Province, Xiaokuan was sent back to his former post.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu pacified Jin Province, he again ordered Xiaokuan back to his old garrison.

value.zh: 趙善字僧慶，太傅、楚國公貴之從祖兄也。
value.en: Zhao Shan, courtesy name Sengqing, was a senior cousin of Yuwen Gui, grand tutor and Duke of Chu.
value.literal: Zhao Shan, styled Sengqing, was a paternal cousin once removed of the Grand Tutor and Duke of Chu, Gui.

value.zh: 祖國，魏龍驤將軍、洛州刺史。
value.en: His grandfather Guo had served Wei as general of dragon cavalry and inspector of Luo Province.
value.literal: His grandfather Guo was Wei General of Dragon Cavalry and Inspector of Luo Province.

value.zh: 父更，安樂太守。
value.en: His father Geng was administrator of Anle commandery.
value.literal: His father Geng was Administrator of Anle commandery.

value.zh: 天和六年，出為汾州諸軍事、汾州刺史，進爵為公，增邑一千五百戶。
value.en: In the sixth year of Tianhe he was sent out as area commander of military affairs for Fen Province and governor of Fen, raised to duke, and given an added fief of one thousand five hundred households.
value.literal: In the sixth year of Tianhe, he went out as area commander of military affairs for Fen Province and Governor of Fen Province; he was advanced in rank to duke, and his fief was increased by one thousand five hundred households.

value.zh: 齊將段孝先率衆五萬來寇，梯沖地道，晝夜攻城。
value.en: Northern Qi general Duan Xiaoxian led fifty thousand men against the city with siege towers, rams, and underground tunnels, attacking day and night.
value.literal: Qi general Duan Xiaoxian led a host of fifty thousand to invade; with scaling ladders, rams, and underground tunnels, they assaulted the city day and night.

value.zh: 敷親當矢石，隨事扞禦，拒守累旬。
value.en: Fu met arrows and stones in person, met each assault as it came, and held out for many weeks.
value.literal: Fu personally faced arrows and stones, resisted according to each circumstance, and held out for many tens of days.

value.zh: 孝先攻之愈急。
value.en: Duan Xiaoxian pressed the attack ever harder.
value.literal: Xiaoxian attacked all the more urgently.

value.zh: 時城中兵不滿二千，戰死者已十四五，糧儲又盡，公私窮蹙。
value.en: The garrison held fewer than two thousand men; four or five men in ten had already fallen; grain was gone, and public stores and private households alike were desperate.
value.literal: At the time the troops in the city numbered fewer than two thousand; those killed in battle already reached four or five tenths; grain stores were again exhausted, and public and private both were in desperate straits.

value.zh: 齊公憲總兵赴救，憚孝先，不敢進軍。
value.en: Duke of Qi Yuwen Xian marched to the relief but feared Duan Xiaoxian and would not press forward.
value.literal: Duke of Qi Xian mustered troops to go to the rescue, but feared Xiaoxian and did not dare advance.

value.zh: 敷知必陷沒，乃召其衆謂之曰：「吾與卿等，俱在邊鎮，實願同心戮力，破賊全城。
value.en: Knowing the city could not hold, Fu gathered his men and said, "You and I stand together on the frontier; I had hoped we might unite and break the enemy to save this city.
value.literal: Fu knew the city must fall, so he summoned his men and said to them: "You and I together are stationed on the frontier; I truly wish to join hearts and combine strength to break the enemy and preserve the whole city.

value.zh: 但強寇四面攻圍日久，吾等糧食已盡，救援斷絕。
value.en: But a strong foe has besieged us from every side for days; our grain is spent and no relief will come.
value.literal: But strong enemies have attacked from all sides for many days; our grain is already exhausted, and relief is cut off.

value.zh: 守死窮城，非丈夫也。
value.en: To die defending a doomed city is no true man's course.
value.literal: To hold out and die in a hopeless city is not the act of a true man.

value.zh: 今勝兵之士，猶數百人，欲突圍出戰，死生一決。
value.en: We still have several hundred able fighters; I mean to break out and fight, staking life and death on a single charge.
value.literal: Today the fit fighting men still number several hundred; I wish to break through the siege and go out to fight, settling life and death in one decision.

value.zh: 儻或得免，猶冀生還，受罪闕庭，孰與死於寇乎！
value.en: If we can break free, some of us may yet live, return home, and accept judgment at court—better that than dying at the enemy's hands!
value.literal: If by chance we may escape, we may still hope to return alive, receive punishment before the imperial court — how is that not better than dying at the hands of the enemy!

value.zh: 吾計決矣，於諸君意何如？」
value.en: My mind is made up. What say you?"
value.literal: My decision is made — what do you all think?"

value.zh: 衆咸涕泣從命。
value.en: All wept and agreed to follow him.
value.literal: All wept and, weeping, obeyed.

value.zh: 敷乃率見兵夜出，擊殺齊軍數十人。
value.en: That night Fu led his remaining men out and killed several dozen Qi soldiers.
value.literal: Fu then led the troops available and went out by night, killing several tens of Qi soldiers.

value.zh: 齊軍衆稍卻。
value.en: The Qi ranks fell back a little.
value.literal: The Qi army masses withdrew slightly.

value.zh: 俄而孝先率諸軍盡銳圍之，敷殊死戰，矢盡，為孝先所擒。
value.en: Soon Duan Xiaoxian closed in with every available man; Fu fought to the last; when his arrows were spent he was taken.
value.literal: Before long Xiaoxian led all the armies with full sharpness to surround them; Fu fought to the death; arrows exhausted, he was captured by Xiaoxian.

value.zh: 齊人方欲任用之，敷不為之屈，遂以憂懼卒於鄴。
value.en: The Qi meant to win him over, but Fu would not yield and died in Ye of grief and anguish.
value.literal: The men of Qi were just then intending to employ him, but Fu would not submit to them; he thereupon died in Ye from grief and fear.

value.zh: 高祖平齊，贈使持節、大將軍、淮廣復三州諸軍事、三州刺史，諡曰忠壯。
value.en: After Emperor Wu pacified Qi, Fu was posthumously made bearer of the staff, grand general, area commander of military affairs for Huai, Guang, and Fu provinces, governor of those three provinces, and given the posthumous name Zhongzhuang.
value.literal: When the High Ancestor pacified Qi, he was posthumously granted bearer of the staff, Grand General, military affairs for Huai, Guang, and Fu three provinces, Governor of three provinces, and the posthumous name Loyal and Robust.

value.zh: 葬於華陰舊塋。
value.en: He was buried in the family graveyard at Huayin.
value.literal: He was buried at the old family graves at Huayin.

value.zh: 起旃蒙協洽，盡柔兆敦牂，凡十二年。
value.en: From Zhanmeng Xiehe through Rouzhao Dunjiang—twelve years in all.
value.literal: From Zhanmeng Xiehe through Rouzhao Dunjiang; twelve years in all.

value.zh: 夏，益州夷二十四邑、三萬餘人皆反。
value.en: In summer the Yi of Yizhou—twenty-four settlements and more than thirty thousand people—all rebelled.
value.literal: In summer, the Yi of Yizhou—twenty-four settlements and more than thirty thousand people—all rebelled.

value.zh: 遣水衡都尉呂辟胡募吏民及發犍為、蜀郡奔命往擊，大破之。
value.en: Chief Steward for Water and Parks Lü Pihu was sent to recruit officials and commoners and raise emergency levies from Qianwei and Shu to attack them; he won a crushing victory.
value.literal: The Chief Steward for Water and Parks Lü Pihu was sent to recruit officials and commoners and to raise emergency levies from Qianwei and Shu commanderies to attack them; he inflicted a great defeat.

value.zh: 秋，七月，赦天下。
value.en: In autumn, the seventh month, an amnesty was proclaimed for all under Heaven.
value.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, an amnesty was proclaimed for all under Heaven.

value.zh: 大雨，至於十月，渭橋絕。
value.en: Heavy rain lasted until the tenth month; the Wei River bridge was washed out.
value.literal: Heavy rain lasted until the tenth month; the Wei River bridge was cut off.

value.zh: 武帝初崩，賜諸侯王璽書。
value.en: When Emperor Wu first died, imperial-seal letters of appointment were sent to the feudal kings.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu first died, imperial-seal letters of appointment were bestowed on the feudal kings.

value.zh: 燕王旦得書不肯哭，曰：「璽書封小，京師疑有變。」
value.en: Prince Dan of Yan received the letter and refused to mourn, saying, "The seal on the letter is small—the capital may suspect something has changed."
value.literal: The Prince of Yan, Dan, received the letter and refused to mourn, saying: "The seal on the letter is small; the capital suspects there has been a change."

value.zh: 遣幸臣壽西長、孫縱之、王孺等之長安，以問禮儀為名，陰刺候朝廷事。
value.en: He sent favored retainers Shou Xichang, Sun Zongzhi, Wang Ru, and others to Chang'an, ostensibly to inquire about ritual, but secretly to spy on affairs at court.
value.literal: He sent favored retainers Shou Xichang, Sun Zongzhi, Wang Ru, and others to Chang'an, under the pretext of inquiring about ritual, to spy secretly on affairs at court.

value.zh: 及有詔褒賜旦錢三十萬，益封萬三千戶，旦怒曰：「我當為帝，何賜也！」
value.en: When an edict came praising and rewarding Dan with three hundred thousand cash and an additional enfeoffment of thirteen thousand households, Dan raged, "I ought to be emperor—what is this reward!"
value.literal: When an edict came praising and rewarding Dan with three hundred thousand cash and an additional enfeoffment of thirteen thousand households, Dan angrily said: "I ought to be emperor—what is this reward!"

value.zh: 遂與宗室中山哀王子長、齊孝王孫澤等結謀，詐言以武帝時受詔，得職吏事，修武備，備非常。
value.en: He thereupon conspired with the imperial clansman Chang, son of King Ai of Zhongshan, Sun Ze, grandson of King Xiao of Qi, and others, falsely claiming that in Emperor Wu's time he had received an edict empowering him to manage officials, repair armaments, and guard against the unexpected.
value.literal: He thereupon joined in conspiracy with the imperial clansman Chang, son of King Ai of Zhongshan, Sun Ze, grandson of King Xiao of Qi, and others, falsely claiming that in Emperor Wu's time he had received an edict empowering him to manage officials and affairs, repair armaments, and guard against the unexpected.

value.zh: 郎中成軫謂旦曰：「大王失職，獨可起而索，不可坐而得也。
value.en: Palace Gentleman Cheng Zhen told Dan, "Your Highness has lost your place; you can only rise and demand it—you cannot sit and obtain it.
value.literal: Palace Gentleman Cheng Zhen said to Dan: "Your Highness has lost your post; you can only rise and demand it—you cannot sit and obtain it.

value.zh: 大王壹起，國中雖女子皆奮臂隨大王。」
value.en: If Your Highness rises once, throughout the state even women will take up arms and follow you."
value.literal: If Your Highness rises once, throughout the state even women will swing their arms and follow Your Highness."

value.zh: 旦即與澤謀，為奸書，言：「少帝非武帝子，大臣所共立；
value.en: Dan at once plotted with Ze and forged a seditious letter, saying, "The young emperor is not Emperor Wu's son; the great ministers jointly established him;
value.literal: Dan at once plotted with Ze and forged a wicked letter, saying: "The young emperor is not Emperor Wu's son; the great ministers jointly established him;

value.zh: 天下宜共伐之！」
value.en: all under Heaven ought jointly to attack him!"
value.literal: all under Heaven ought jointly to attack him!"

value.zh: 使人傳行郡國以搖動百姓。
value.en: He sent men to circulate it through the commanderies and kingdoms to stir up the people.
value.literal: He sent men to circulate it through the commanderies and kingdoms to stir up the people.

value.zh: 澤謀歸發兵臨菑，殺青州刺史雋不疑。
value.en: Ze plotted to return, raise troops, advance on Zi, and kill Qingzhou Inspector Juan Buyi.
value.literal: Ze plotted to return, raise troops, advance on Zi, and kill Qingzhou Inspector Juan Buyi.

value.zh: 旦招來郡國奸人，賦斂銅鐵作甲兵，數閱其車騎、材官卒，發民大獵以講士馬，須期日。
value.en: Dan gathered wicked men from the commanderies and kingdoms, levied copper and iron for armor and weapons, repeatedly reviewed his chariots, cavalry, and skilled troops, and mobilized the people for great hunts to drill men and horses, awaiting the appointed day.
value.literal: Dan gathered wicked men from the commanderies and kingdoms, levied copper and iron to make armor and weapons, repeatedly reviewed his chariots, cavalry, and skilled soldiers, and mobilized the people for great hunts to drill troops and horses, awaiting the appointed day.

value.zh: 郎中韓義等數諫旦，旦殺義等凡十五人。
value.en: Palace Gentlemen Han Yi and others repeatedly admonished Dan; Dan killed Yi and fourteen others—fifteen in all.
value.literal: Palace Gentlemen Han Yi and others repeatedly admonished Dan; Dan killed Yi and the rest, fifteen in all.

value.zh: 會缾侯成知澤等謀，以告雋不疑。
value.en: Marquis of Ping Cheng learned of Ze's plot and reported it to Juan Buyi.
value.literal: It happened that Marquis of Ping Cheng learned of Ze's plot and reported it to Juan Buyi.

value.zh: 八月，不疑收捕澤等以聞。
value.en: In the eighth month Buyi arrested Ze and the others and reported it.
value.literal: In the eighth month, Buyi arrested Ze and the others and reported it.

value.zh: 天子遣大鴻臚丞治，連引燕王。
value.en: The emperor sent the Grand Herald's assistant to investigate, implicating the Prince of Yan in succession.
value.literal: The Son of Heaven sent the Grand Herald's assistant to investigate, implicating the Prince of Yan in succession.

value.zh: 有詔，以燕王至親，勿治；
value.en: An edict stated that because the Prince of Yan was a close kinsman, he was not to be prosecuted;
value.literal: An edict stated that because the Prince of Yan was a close kinsman, he was not to be prosecuted;

value.zh: 而澤等皆伏誅。
value.en: but Ze and the others were all executed.
value.literal: but Ze and the others were all executed.

value.zh: 遷雋不疑為京兆尹。
value.en: Juan Buyi was transferred to Metropolitan Commandant.
value.literal: Juan Buyi was transferred to be Metropolitan Commandant.

value.zh: 不疑為京兆尹，吏民敬其威信。
value.en: As Metropolitan Commandant, Buyi won respect from officials and commoners for his authority and trustworthiness.
value.literal: As Metropolitan Commandant, Buyi was respected by officials and commoners for his authority and trustworthiness.

value.zh: 每行縣、錄囚徒還，其母輒問不疑：「有所平反？
value.en: Whenever he toured the counties and returned from reviewing prisoners, his mother would ask Buyi, "Were any cases reversed?
value.literal: Whenever he toured the counties and returned from recording prisoners, his mother would ask Buyi: "Were any cases reversed?

value.zh: 活幾何人？」
value.en: How many people were spared?"
value.literal: How many people were spared?"

value.zh: 即不疑多有所平反，母喜笑異於他時；
value.en: If Buyi had reversed many cases, his mother would laugh with joy unlike at other times;
value.literal: If Buyi had reversed many cases, his mother would laugh with joy unlike at other times;

value.zh: 或無所出，母怒，為不食。
value.en: if there were none, his mother grew angry and refused to eat.
value.literal: if there were none, his mother grew angry and would not eat.

value.zh: 故不疑為吏，嚴而不殘。
value.en: For this reason Buyi as an official was stern but not cruel.
value.literal: For this reason Buyi as an official was stern but not cruel.

value.zh: 九月，丙子，秺敬侯金日磾薨。
value.en: In the ninth month, on bingzi, Marquis Jing of Di Jin Midi died.
value.literal: In the ninth month, on bingzi, Marquis Jing of Di Jin Midi died.

value.zh: 初，武帝病，有遺詔，封金日磾為秺侯，上官桀為安陽侯，霍光為博陸侯；
value.en: At the outset, when Emperor Wu was ill, a testamentary edict enfeoffed Jin Midi as Marquis of Di, Shangguan Jie as Marquis of Anyang, and Huo Guang as Marquis of Bolu;
value.literal: At the outset, when Emperor Wu was ill, there was a testamentary edict enfeoffing Jin Midi as Marquis of Di, Shangguan Jie as Marquis of Anyang, and Huo Guang as Marquis of Bolu;

value.zh: 皆以前捕反者馬何羅等功封。
value.en: all were enfeoffed for their former merit in capturing the rebel Ma Heluo and others.
value.literal: all were enfeoffed for their former merit in capturing the rebel Ma Heluo and others.

value.zh: 日磾以帝少，不受封，光等亦不敢受。
value.en: Midi, because the emperor was young, did not accept the enfeoffment; Guang and the others also did not dare accept.
value.literal: Midi, because the emperor was young, did not accept the enfeoffment; Guang and the others also did not dare accept.

value.zh: 及日磾病困，光白封，日磾臥受印綬；
value.en: When Midi's illness grew critical, Guang reported and enfeoffed him; Midi received the seal and ribbon while lying down;
value.literal: When Midi's illness grew critical, Guang reported and enfeoffed him; Midi received the seal and ribbon while lying down;

value.zh: 一日薨。
value.en: and died the next day.
value.literal: and died the next day.

value.zh: 日磾兩子賞、建俱侍中，與帝略同年，共臥起。
value.en: Midi's two sons Shang and Jian were both Palace Attendants, roughly the emperor's age, sharing bed and rising with him.
value.literal: Midi's two sons Shang and Jian were both Palace Attendants, roughly the emperor's age, sharing bed and rising together.

value.zh: 賞為奉車，建駙馬都尉。
value.en: Shang was Director of the Imperial Carriage; Jian was Commandant of the Palace Steeds.
value.literal: Shang was Director of the Imperial Carriage; Jian was Commandant of the Palace Steeds.

value.zh: 及賞嗣侯，佩兩綬，上謂霍將軍曰：「金氏兄弟兩人，不可使俱兩綬邪？」
value.en: When Shang succeeded to the marquisate and wore two ribbons, the emperor said to General Huo, "The two Jin brothers—could they not both wear two ribbons?"
value.literal: When Shang succeeded to the marquisate and wore two ribbons, the emperor said to General Huo: "The two Jin brothers—could they not both wear two ribbons?"

value.zh: 對曰：「賞自嗣父為侯耳。」
value.en: He replied, "Shang has merely succeeded his father as marquis."
value.literal: He replied: "Shang has merely succeeded his father as marquis."

value.zh: 上笑曰：「侯不在我與將軍乎？」
value.en: The emperor laughed and said, "Are marquisates not in my hands and yours?"
value.literal: The emperor laughed and said: "Are marquisates not in my hands and the general's?"

value.zh: 對曰：「先帝之約，有功乃得封侯。」
value.en: He replied, "The former emperor's covenant: only with merit may one be enfeoffed as marquis."
value.literal: He replied: "The former emperor's covenant: only with merit may one be enfeoffed as marquis."

value.zh: 遂止。
value.en: The matter thereupon ceased.
value.literal: The matter thereupon ceased.

value.zh: 閏月，遣故廷尉王平等五人持節行郡國，舉賢良，問民疾苦、冤、失職者。
value.en: In the intercalary month, former Minister of Justice Wang Ping and five others were sent with credentials to tour the commanderies and kingdoms, recommend the worthy and good, and inquire into popular suffering, wrongs, and dereliction of duty.
value.literal: In the intercalary month, the former Minister of Justice Wang Ping and five others were sent with credentials to tour the commanderies and kingdoms, recommend the worthy and good, and inquire into the people's suffering, wrongs, and dereliction of duty.

value.zh: 冬，無冰。
value.en: In winter there was no ice.
value.literal: In winter, there was no ice.

value.zh: 春，正月，封大將軍光為博陸侯，左將軍桀為安陽侯。
value.en: In spring, the first month, Grand General Guang was enfeoffed as Marquis of Bolu and Left General Jie as Marquis of Anyang.
value.literal: In spring, the first month, Grand General Guang was enfeoffed as Marquis of Bolu and Left General Jie as Marquis of Anyang.

value.zh: 或說霍光曰：「將軍不見諸呂之事乎？
value.en: Someone said to Huo Guang, "General, have you not seen what befell the Lü clan?
value.literal: Someone said to Huo Guang: "General, have you not seen what befell the Lü clan?

value.zh: 處伊尹、周公之位，攝政擅權，而背宗室，不與共職，是以天下不信，卒至於滅亡。
value.en: Occupying the positions of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou, holding regency and monopolizing power, yet turning your back on the imperial clan and not sharing office with them—for this reason the realm did not trust them, and they ended in extinction.
value.literal: Occupying the positions of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou, holding regency and monopolizing power, yet turning your back on the imperial clan and not sharing office with them—for this reason all under Heaven did not trust them, and they ended in extinction.

value.zh: 今將軍當盛位，帝春秋富，宜納宗室，又多與大臣共事，反諸呂道。
value.en: Now you occupy a flourishing position and the emperor is still young; you ought to bring in the imperial clan and share many affairs with the great ministers—reversing the Lü path.
value.literal: Now the general occupies a flourishing position and the emperor's years are still rich; you ought to bring in the imperial clan and share many affairs with the great ministers—reversing the way of the Lü.

value.zh: 如是，則可以免患。」
value.en: If so, you may escape calamity."
value.literal: If so, you may escape calamity."

value.zh: 光然之，乃擇宗室可用者，遂拜楚元王孫辟疆及宗室劉長樂皆為光祿大夫，辟疆守長樂衛尉。
value.en: Guang assented; he selected usable members of the imperial clan and appointed King Yuan of Chu's grandson Pijiang and clansman Liu Changle both Palace Grandees, with Pijiang serving as Commandant of the Guards for Changle.
value.literal: Guang assented; he thereupon selected usable members of the imperial clan and appointed the grandson of King Yuan of Chu, Pijiang, and the clansman Liu Changle both as Palace Grandees, with Pijiang holding office as Commandant of the Guards for Changle.

value.zh: 三月，遣使者振貸貧民無種、食者。
value.en: In the third month envoys were sent to relieve and lend to poor commoners without seed or food.
value.literal: In the third month, envoys were sent to relieve and lend to poor commoners without seed or food.

value.zh: 秋，八月，詔曰：「往年災害多，今年蠶、麥傷，所振貸種、食勿收責，毋令民出今年田租。」
value.en: In autumn, the eighth month, an edict said, "Disasters were many in former years; this year silkworms and wheat were harmed. Do not collect repayment for the seed and food that were relieved and lent; do not make the people pay this year's field tax."
value.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, an edict said: "In former years disasters were many; this year silkworms and wheat were harmed. The seed and food that were relieved and lent—do not collect repayment; do not make the people pay this year's field tax."

value.zh: 初，武帝征伐匈奴，深入窮追，二十餘年，匈奴馬畜孕重墮殰，罷極，苦之。
value.en: At the outset Emperor Wu campaigned against the Xiongnu, driving deep in relentless pursuit for more than twenty years; Xiongnu horses and livestock, pregnant and heavy, miscarried and perished; exhausted to the limit, they suffered bitterly.
value.literal: At the outset, Emperor Wu campaigned against the Xiongnu, driving deep in relentless pursuit for more than twenty years; the Xiongnu's horses and livestock, pregnant and heavy, miscarried and perished; exhausted to the limit, they suffered bitterly.

value.zh: 常有欲和親意，未能得。
value.en: They often wished for heqin peace but could not achieve it.
value.literal: They often had the intent to seek heqin peace but could not achieve it.

value.zh: 狐鹿孤單于有異母弟為左大都尉，賢，國人鄉之，母閼氏恐單于不立子而立左大都尉也，乃私使殺之。
value.en: Chanyu Hulu Gu had a younger half-brother who was Left Grand Commandant and worthy; the people looked toward him. The chanyu's mother, the Yanzhi consort, feared the chanyu would not establish his son but would establish the Left Grand Commandant, and secretly had him killed.
value.literal: The chanyu Hulu Gu had a younger half-brother who was Left Grand Commandant, worthy; the people of the state looked toward him. The chanyu's mother, the Yanzhi consort, feared the chanyu would not establish his son but would establish the Left Grand Commandant, and secretly had him killed.

value.zh: 左大都尉同母兄怨，遂不肯復會單于庭。
value.en: The Left Grand Commandant's elder brother by the same mother bore resentment and refused to attend the chanyu's court again.
value.literal: The Left Grand Commandant's elder brother by the same mother bore resentment and thereupon refused to attend the chanyu's court again.

value.zh: 是歲，單于病且死，謂諸貴人：「我子少，不能治國，立弟右谷蠡王。」
value.en: That year the chanyu was ill and near death; he told the nobles, "My son is young and cannot govern the state; establish my younger brother, the Right Guli King."
value.literal: That year the chanyu was ill and near death; he told the nobles: "My son is young and cannot govern the state; establish my younger brother, the Right Guli King."

value.zh: 及單于死，衛律等與顓渠閼氏謀，匿其喪，矯單于令，更立子左谷蠡王為壺衍鞮單于。
value.en: When the chanyu died, Wei Lü and others plotted with Zhuanqu Yanzhi, concealed his death, forged the chanyu's command, and instead established his son, the Left Guli King, as Chanyu Huyandi.
value.literal: When the chanyu died, Wei Lü and others plotted with Zhuanqu Yanzhi, concealed his death, forged the chanyu's command, and instead established his son, the Left Guli King, as chanyu Huyandi.

value.zh: 左賢王、右谷蠡王怨望，率其眾欲南歸漢，恐不能自致，即脅盧屠王，欲與西降烏孫。
value.en: The Left Worthy King and the Right Guli King harbored resentment; they led their followers wishing to return south to Han, fearing they could not reach it on their own, and coerced the Lutu King, intending to surrender west to the Wusun.
value.literal: The Left Worthy King and the Right Guli King harbored resentment; they led their followers wishing to return south to Han, fearing they could not reach it on their own, and thereupon coerced the Lutu King, intending to descend west and surrender to the Wusun.

value.zh: 盧屠王告之單于，使人驗問，右谷蠡王不服，反以其罪罪盧屠王，國人皆冤之。
value.en: The Lutu King reported it to the chanyu; investigators were sent. The Right Guli King would not submit and instead charged the Lutu King with that very crime; the people all considered it unjust.
value.literal: The Lutu King reported it to the chanyu; men were sent to investigate and question. The Right Guli King would not submit and instead charged the Lutu King with that very crime; the people of the state all considered it unjust.

value.zh: 於是二王去居其所，不復肯會龍城，匈奴始衰。
value.en: Thereupon the two kings departed to their own territories and would no longer attend at Dragon City; the Xiongnu began to decline.
value.literal: Thereupon the two kings departed to dwell in their own places and would no longer attend at Dragon City; the Xiongnu began to decline.

value.zh: 春，正月，追尊帝外祖趙父為順成侯。
value.en: In spring, the first month, the emperor's maternal grandfather, Father Zhao, was posthumously honored as Marquis of Shuncheng.
value.literal: In spring, the first month, the emperor's maternal grandfather, Father Zhao, was posthumously honored as Marquis of Shuncheng.

value.zh: 順成侯有姊君姁，賜錢二百萬、奴婢、第宅以充實焉。
value.en: Marquis of Shuncheng had an elder sister, Junxu; she was granted two million cash, slaves and maidservants, and a mansion to enrich her establishment.
value.literal: Marquis of Shuncheng had an elder sister, Junxu; she was granted two million cash, slaves and maidservants, and a mansion to enrich her establishment.

value.zh: 諸昆弟各以親疏受賞賜，無在位者。
value.en: The various siblings each received rewards according to closeness of kin; none held office.
value.literal: The various brothers and sisters each received rewards according to closeness of kin; none held office.

value.zh: 有男子乘黃犢車詣北闕，自謂衛太子；
value.en: A man riding a yellow calf-drawn carriage came to the Northern Gate Tower and declared himself Crown Prince Wei;
value.literal: A man riding a yellow calf-drawn carriage came to the Northern Gate Tower and declared himself the Heir of Wei;

value.zh: 公車以聞。
value.en: the Imperial Carriage Office reported it.
value.literal: the Imperial Carriage Office reported it.

value.zh: 詔使公、卿、將軍、中二千石雜識視。
value.en: An edict ordered dukes, ministers, generals, and officials at two thousand bushels and above jointly to identify and examine him.
value.literal: An edict ordered the dukes, ministers, generals, and officials at two thousand bushels and above jointly to identify and examine him.

value.zh: 長安中吏民聚觀者數萬人。
value.en: Tens of thousands of Chang'an officials and commoners gathered to watch.
value.literal: Officials and commoners of Chang'an gathered to watch—tens of thousands.

value.zh: 右將軍勒兵闕下以備非常。
value.en: The Right General arrayed troops below the gate tower to guard against the unexpected.
value.literal: The Right General arrayed troops below the gate tower to guard against the unexpected.

value.zh: 丞相、御史、中二千石至者並莫敢發言。
value.en: The chancellor, censor, and officials at two thousand bushels and above who arrived all dared not speak.
value.literal: The chancellor, censor, and officials at two thousand bushels and above who arrived all did not dare speak.

value.zh: 京兆尹不疑後到，叱從吏收縛。
value.en: Metropolitan Commandant Buyi arrived later and shouted at his clerks to seize and bind him.
value.literal: Metropolitan Commandant Buyi arrived later and shouted at his attending clerks to seize and bind him.

value.zh: 或曰：「是非未可知，且安之。」
value.en: Someone said, "Whether this is true or false is not yet known; for now let him be."
value.literal: Someone said: "Whether this is true or false is not yet known; for now let him be at ease."

value.zh: 不疑曰：「諸君何患於衛太子！
value.en: Buyi said, "Why do you gentlemen worry about Crown Prince Wei!
value.literal: Buyi said: "Why do you gentlemen worry about the Heir of Wei!

value.zh: 昔蒯聵違命出奔，輒距而不納，《春秋》是之。
value.en: In former times Kuai Kui disobeyed orders and fled abroad; Ji Zhe barred him and would not admit him—the Spring and Autumn Annals approves this.
value.literal: In former times Kuai Kui disobeyed orders and fled abroad; Ji Zhe barred him and would not admit him—the Spring and Autumn Annals approves this.

value.zh: 衛太子得罪先帝，亡不即死，今來自詣，此罪人也！」
value.en: Crown Prince Wei offended the former emperor, fled and did not die at once; now he has come of his own accord—this man is a criminal!"
value.literal: The Heir of Wei offended the former emperor, fled and did not die at once; now he has come of his own accord—this man is a criminal!"

value.zh: 遂送詔獄。
value.en: He was thereupon sent to the imperial prison under edict.
value.literal: He was thereupon sent to the imperial prison under edict.

value.zh: 天子與大將軍霍光聞而嘉之曰：「公卿大臣當用有經術、明於大誼者。」
value.en: The emperor and Grand General Huo Guang heard of it and praised him, saying, "Dukes, ministers, and great officials ought to employ those versed in the classics and clear on great principle."
value.literal: The Son of Heaven and Grand General Huo Guang heard of it and praised him, saying: "Dukes, ministers, and great officials ought to employ those versed in the classics and clear on great principle."

value.zh: 繇是不疑名聲重於朝廷，在位者皆自以不及也。
value.en: From this Buyi's reputation weighed heavy at court; those in office all considered themselves his inferior.
value.literal: From this Buyi's reputation weighed heavy in court; those in office all considered themselves his inferior.

value.zh: 廷尉驗治何人，竟得奸詐，本夏陽人，姓成，名方遂，居湖，以卜筮為事。
value.en: The Minister of Justice investigated: who was this man? At last the fraud was exposed. He was originally from Xiayang, surname Cheng, personal name Fang Sui, living at Hu, who made his living by divination.
value.literal: The Minister of Justice investigated and tried: who was this man? At last the fraud was obtained. He was originally a man of Xiayang, surname Cheng, personal name Fang Sui, dwelling at Hu, who made divination by milfoil and tortoise his trade.

value.zh: 有故太子舍人嘗從方遂卜，謂曰：「子狀貌甚似衛太子。」
value.en: A former crown prince's palace attendant had once had Fang Sui divine for him and said, "Your appearance greatly resembles Crown Prince Wei."
value.literal: A former Palace Attendant of the heir had once had Fang Sui divine for him and said to him: "Your appearance greatly resembles the Heir of Wei."

value.zh: 方遂心利其言，冀得以富貴。
value.en: Fang Sui's heart seized on his words and hoped thereby to gain wealth and rank.
value.literal: Fang Sui's heart profited by his words and hoped thereby to gain wealth and rank.

value.zh: 坐誣罔不道，要斬。
value.en: Convicted of false accusation and impiety, he was beheaded at the waist.
value.literal: Convicted of false accusation and impiety, he was beheaded at the waist.

value.zh: 夏，六月，封上官安為桑樂侯。
value.en: In summer, the sixth month, Shangguan An was enfeoffed as Marquis of Sangle.
value.literal: In summer, the sixth month, Shangguan An was enfeoffed as Marquis of Sangle.

value.zh: 安日以驕淫，受賜殿中，對賓客言：「與我婿飲，大樂！」
value.en: An grew daily more arrogant and dissolute; receiving gifts in the palace hall, he said to guests, "Drink with my son-in-law—what joy!"
value.literal: An daily grew arrogant and dissolute; receiving gifts in the palace hall, he said to guests: "Drink with my son-in-law—great joy!"

value.zh: 見其服飾，使人歸，欲自燒物。
value.en: Seeing their clothing and adornments, he had people go home, intending to burn their possessions.
value.literal: Seeing their clothing and adornments, he had people return home, wishing to burn their possessions.

value.zh: 子病死，仰而罵天。
value.en: When his son died of illness, he looked up and cursed Heaven.
value.literal: When his son died of illness, he looked up and cursed Heaven.

value.zh: 其頑悖如此。
value.en: His obstinate perversity was like this.
value.literal: His obstinate perversity was like this.

value.zh: 罷儋耳、真番郡。
value.en: The Dan'er and Zhenfan commanderies were abolished.
value.literal: The Dan'er and Zhenfan commanderies were abolished.

value.zh: 秋，大鴻臚廣明、軍正王平擊益州，斬首、捕虜三萬餘人，獲畜產五萬餘頭。
value.en: In autumn, Grand Herald Guangming and Army Rectifier Wang Ping attacked Yizhou, beheading and capturing more than thirty thousand men and taking more than fifty thousand head of livestock.
value.literal: In autumn, Grand Herald Guangming and Army Rectifier Wang Ping attacked Yizhou; heads cut off and captives taken exceeded thirty thousand, and livestock obtained exceeded fifty thousand head.

value.zh: 諫大夫杜延年見國家承武帝奢侈、師旅之後，數為大將軍光言：「年歲比不登，流民未盡還，宜修孝文時政，示以儉約、寬和，順天心，說民意，年歲宜應。」
value.en: Remonstrance Grandee Du Yannian, seeing the state inherit Emperor Wu's extravagance and campaigns, repeatedly told Grand General Guang, "Harvests have failed year after year and displaced people have not all returned. It is fitting to restore Emperor Wen's policies, show frugality, restraint, lenience, and harmony, accord with Heaven's heart, please the people, and the years ought to respond."
value.literal: Remonstrance Grandee Du Yannian, seeing the state inherit Emperor Wu's extravagance and campaigns, repeatedly spoke to Grand General Guang: "Years in succession have not had good harvests; displaced people have not all returned—it is fitting to restore Emperor Wen's policies, show frugality and restraint and lenience and harmony, accord with Heaven's heart, please the people's intent, and the years ought to respond."

value.zh: 光納其言。
value.en: Guang accepted his counsel.
value.literal: Guang accepted his words.

value.zh: 延年，故御史大夫周之子也。
value.en: Yannian was a son of the former Censor-in-Chief Du Zhou.
value.literal: Yannian was a son of the former Censor-in-Chief Zhou.

value.zh: 春，二月，詔有司問郡國所舉賢良、文學，民所疾苦、教化之要，皆對：「願罷鹽、鐵、酒榷、均輸官，毋與天下爭利，示以儉節，然後教化可興。」
value.en: In spring, the second month, an edict had the responsible offices question the worthy and learned men recommended by commanderies and kingdoms on the people's hardships and the essentials of moral instruction. All replied, "We wish to abolish the salt, iron, wine monopoly, and equalizing transport offices, stop contending with all under Heaven for profit, show frugality and restraint, and only then can moral instruction flourish."
value.literal: In spring, the second month, an edict had the responsible offices question the worthy and learned men recommended by commanderies and kingdoms on the people's hardships and essentials of instruction and transformation; all replied: "We wish to abolish the salt, iron, wine monopoly, and equalizing transport offices, not contend with all under Heaven for profit, show frugality and restraint, and only then can instruction and transformation be raised."

value.zh: 桑弘羊難，以為：「此國家大業，所以制四夷，安邊足用之本，不可廢也。」
value.en: Sang Hongyang objected, saying, "This is the state's great enterprise, the foundation for controlling the four barbarians and securing the borders with sufficient resources—it cannot be abolished."
value.literal: Sang Hongyang objected, holding: "This is the state's great enterprise, the foundation for controlling the four barbarians and securing the borders with sufficient resources—it cannot be abolished."

value.zh: 於是鹽鐵之議起焉。
value.en: Thereupon the salt-and-iron debate arose.
value.literal: Thereupon the salt-and-iron debate arose.

value.zh: 初，蘇武既徙北海上，稟食不至，掘野鼠、去草實而食之。
value.en: At first, after Su Wu had been relocated to the North Sea coast, allotted food did not arrive; he dug up wild rats and stripped grass seeds to eat.
value.literal: At first, after Su Wu had been relocated to the North Sea coast, allotted food did not arrive; he dug wild rats and removed grass seeds and ate them.

value.zh: 杖漢節牧羊，臥起操持，節旄盡落。
value.en: Leaning on the Han staff of office he herded sheep; whether lying down or rising he held it in hand, until the tassels on the staff had all fallen off.
value.literal: Leaning on the Han staff of office he herded sheep; lying down and rising he held it in hand—the tassels on the staff all fell off.

value.zh: 武在漢，與李陵俱為侍中；
value.en: In Han, Wu and Li Ling had both served as Palace Attendants;
value.literal: Wu in Han had together with Li Ling served as Palace Attendant;

value.zh: 陵降匈奴，不敢求武。
value.en: Ling surrendered to the Xiongnu and did not dare seek out Wu.
value.literal: Ling surrendered to the Xiongnu and did not dare seek Wu.

value.zh: 久之，單于使陵至海上，為武置酒設樂，因謂武曰：「單于聞陵與子卿素厚，故使來說足下，虛心欲相待，終不得歸漢，空自苦；
value.en: After a long time the Chanyu sent Ling to the sea coast, set out wine and music for Wu, and said to him, "The Chanyu heard that Ling and Ziqing were always close, and therefore sent me to persuade you, my lord. His heart is open and he wishes to treat you well, but in the end you cannot return to Han and only suffer in vain;
value.literal: After long time the Chanyu sent Ling to the sea coast, set out wine and music for Wu, and thereby said to Wu: "The Chanyu heard Ling and Ziqing were always close, therefore sent me to persuade you, my lord—the heart is open and wishes to treat you well; in the end you cannot return to Han and vainly suffer yourself;

value.zh: 亡人之地，信義安所見乎！
value.en: in a land of lost men, where is faith and righteousness to be shown!
value.literal: in a land of lost men, where is faith and righteousness to be shown!

value.zh: 足下兄弟二人，前皆坐事自殺；
value.en: Your lordship's two brothers were both earlier convicted of offenses and killed themselves;
value.literal: Your lordship's two brothers before both sat convicted of offenses and killed themselves;

value.zh: 來時，太夫人已不幸；
value.en: when you came, your mother had already died;
value.literal: when you came, the Grand Lady had already met misfortune;

value.zh: 子卿婦年少，聞已更嫁矣；
value.en: Ziqing's wife is young—I hear she has already remarried;
value.literal: Ziqing's wife is young—I hear she has already remarried;

value.zh: 獨有女弟二人、兩女、一男，今復十餘年，存亡不可知。
value.en: only two younger sisters, two daughters, and one son remain; now more than ten years have passed again, and whether they live or die cannot be known.
value.literal: only two younger sisters, two daughters, and one son remain; now again more than ten years—whether alive or dead cannot be known.

value.zh: 人生如朝露，何久自苦如此！
value.en: Human life is like morning dew—why long suffer yourself like this!
value.literal: Human life is like morning dew—why long suffer yourself like this!
